h1: Textile interest subsidy in Haryana: prepare the annual loan evidence
description: Understand how to organise the loan, repayment and project records needed to assess a Haryana textile interest subsidy claim.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Interest Subsidy: Loan Evidence | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
A textile interest subsidy claim needs evidence about the eligible project and the interest paid on the relevant loan. A loan sanction letter alone cannot establish the annual claim amount. Keep the borrowing, repayment record and project investment connected throughout the claim period.

Haryana's July 2023 interest subsidy notification sets out different provisions for textile MSMEs and textile machine manufacturers. The categories should not be mixed. Its bank certificate format asks for loan, disbursement, repayment and interest information, including the exclusion of penal interest from the certified claim calculation. Read the interest subsidy notification.

The policy and its notified schemes were extended through 18 December 2026 by a May 2025 notification. The extension should be read with the scheme conditions and the dates relevant to the individual project. See the extension notification.

sections.title: Confirm the project category before calculating interest
sections.html:
Describe the manufacturing activity, MSME position, exact location and whether the investment is a new unit or qualifying expansion. Record the date production started and identify the investment financed by the loan.

The Textile Interest Subsidy scheme page explains the scheme route. Do not borrow a percentage, annual cap or benefit period from another textile category. A unit making textile machinery requires a different category check from a unit using that machinery to manufacture textiles.

For an expansion, explain what existed before the project and what changed. The factory's total borrowing is not necessarily the same as the borrowing relevant to the assessed expansion.

sections.title: Build a loan record that can be reconciled
sections.html:
Keep a separate record for each loan proposed for review. Include the sanction letter, amendments, disbursement schedule, account statements and lender details. Describe the purpose of the loan and the assets or work it financed.

Ask the bank for the certificate required by the applicable claim format. Give it the relevant financial year and loan reference. A general interest certificate supplied for accounting purposes may not answer every question in the scheme's prescribed format.

Check the certificate against your accounts. Resolve differences in the borrower name, account number, loan amount, disbursement dates and interest figures before filing. Keep an explanation for corrections instead of silently replacing one version of the record.

sections.title: Distinguish interest from other bank debits
sections.html:
A loan account can contain principal repayments, ordinary interest, penal charges, processing fees and other debits. These are not one interchangeable expense.

For illustration, a statement showing a total debit of ₹12 lakh does not mean ₹12 lakh is interest eligible for assistance. Part may be principal and part may be charges. The claim needs a supported breakdown and the calculation permitted by the scheme, rather than a percentage applied to the whole debit.

If the loan was restructured, refinanced, transferred or irregular during the year, disclose that history. Ask how the actual facts affect the claim. Do not assume a fresh bank certificate removes a scheme condition or a repayment issue.

sections.title: Maintain the project evidence as well as the bank evidence
sections.html:
Keep the relevant enterprise records, approvals, investment schedule and production evidence with the annual claim papers. Record changes in ownership, location, capacity or project assets. A correct interest total cannot repair an unresolved question about the applicant or project.

Set a calendar from the current claim provisions and retain proof of submission. If a deadline may have passed, check any permitted route using the actual facts. Do not assume every delay is condonable.

Textile capital investment subsidy is a separate claim route. Maintain distinct calculations and check the interaction of assistance instead of merging capital expenditure and interest into one unsupported total.

sections.title: Make the review easy to follow
sections.html:
Prepare a one-page summary showing the project, loan, financial year, interest figure, supporting bank certificate and unresolved questions. Seven subsidy application mistakes can help you check the wider file.

title: Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
h1: Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
description: Understand PMEGP’s bank-linked margin-money subsidy for a new micro enterprise and prepare a viable application.
metaTitle: PMEGP: Eligibility & Margin-Money Subsidy | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
PMEGP helps eligible applicants establish new micro enterprises in non-farm activities through bank finance and margin-money subsidy. The business still needs a viable project, the required own contribution and a lender willing to sanction the loan.

Margin money is a back-ended subsidy linked to the financed project. It should not be treated as unrestricted cash available to spend before the enterprise is established.

sections.title: What the published framework supports
sections.html:
The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy is ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for the service or business sector. The applicable subsidy depends on the beneficiary category and whether the location is rural or urban. The published framework provides higher assistance for qualifying special categories.

The lender may consider finance beyond the subsidy-linked ceiling in permitted circumstances, but that does not extend subsidy to the additional amount. Capital expenditure and working capital also have separate constraints within the project cost.

sections.title: A new enterprise must meet the activity rules
sections.html:
The normal new-unit route does not cover an existing business simply seeking reimbursement for earlier expenditure. Earlier government subsidy, the applicant’s eligibility, education requirements for specified project sizes and the scheme’s activity exclusions must be examined before filing.

Describe what the enterprise will manufacture or deliver, which machines and premises it needs, and how it will earn enough to meet operating expenses and loan repayment. A generic project report with an inflated machinery schedule weakens the lending case as well as the subsidy application.

sections.title: Prepare the finance and application together
sections.html:
Assemble identity and category evidence where applicable, the project location, education records where required, quotations, premises arrangements and the funding plan. Separate the proposed assets from working capital and excluded items. The sales and expense assumptions should be explainable from the activity and intended market.

The application proceeds through the official PMEGP process and the relevant implementing agency and bank. Bank appraisal, training or other prescribed steps, implementation and verification are part of the route. A portal submission is not a sanction, and a loan sanction should not be confused with final subsidy adjustment.

For an existing PMEGP loan, retain the sanction, disbursement, margin-money and verification records before assessing any pending adjustment. The exact stage is more useful than a statement that subsidy has “not arrived”.

Read the revised PMEGP guidelines and the Government’s May 2026 PMEGP explanation. Confirm the current application process and applicable financial-year instructions with the implementing agency before committing to a submission schedule.

title: Haryana Gramin Udyogik Vikas Yojna (HGUVY)
h1: Haryana Gramin Udyogik Vikas Yojna (HGUVY)
description: HGUVY explained for rural micro-enterprise investments in Haryana, including location evidence, capital support and historic claim conditions.
metaTitle: HGUVY Haryana: HEEP 2020 Benefits & Legacy Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
HGUVY was Haryana’s HEEP 2020 package for new micro enterprises in rural areas of B, C and D category blocks. It combined capital support, term-loan interest assistance and generator-set assistance. Its rural-location test was specific: the site had to fall under the sole jurisdiction of a village panchayat.

A village name in the postal address is not sufficient evidence of that status. The relevant revenue estate, land records and panchayat jurisdiction must match the enterprise’s actual site.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: How the original package worked
sections.html:
The July 2021 notification provided capital assistance on qualifying plant, machinery and building investment, separate interest support on term borrowing and a generator-set component. Its capital rate was 15%, with different ceilings for general-category and women or SC entrepreneurs. Each component had its own cost and timing basis.

The definition of a new enterprise linked qualifying investment, commercial production or term-loan sanction to the notified period. The unit had to remain in production, and the notification imposed continuing conditions for the assisted investment and generator set.

A particularly important restriction concerned PMEGP: a unit that had received PMEGP subsidy was not entitled to HGUVY benefits other than the specified generator-set component. Do not add the headline benefits from both programmes into one funding plan.

sections.title: Evidence that makes the assessment useful
sections.html:
Prepare the land or registered lease document, site jurisdiction details, Udyam and HUM records, investment schedule and commercial-production chronology. For interest assistance, add the bank sanction, disbursement and interest-paid evidence. For the generator, preserve the invoice, capacity and installation records.

Assess each component separately before submitting the prescribed online claim. Keep the original claim dates and departmental correspondence if this concerns an existing file. Historic entitlement and a new proposal after the policy transition require different advice.

Is every rural business covered?

No. The original scheme applied to new micro enterprises in the specified block categories and required the other conditions to be met. Rural location alone did not decide eligibility.

title: Generator Set Subsidy Scheme in Haryana
h1: Generator Set Subsidy Scheme in Haryana
description: The Haryana generator-set scheme is distinct from PMEGP. Read the historic rural-location, enterprise-size and purchase conditions.
metaTitle: Haryana Generator Set Subsidy: HEEP 2020 Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s Generator Set Subsidy Scheme was notified for small and medium enterprises in rural C and D category blocks under HEEP 2020. It addressed the cost of a generator for continuity of power. It was a separate programme from PMEGP.

The official definition was not restricted to diesel: it described generator sets using diesel, CNG, petrol or other fuels. The machine’s fuel, capacity and operating permissions must therefore be considered alongside its scheme treatment.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: The benefit depended on the enterprise and equipment
sections.html:
The June 2021 notification used a per-kVA amount subject to a percentage of the generator cost, with different percentage limits for small and medium enterprises. That structure means the capacity figure and the purchase price both matter. A larger set does not create an unlimited claim.

The unit had to be in a rural area under village-panchayat jurisdiction and in regular production. The generator had to be bought from an authorised dealer or manufacturer within the applicable period and remain intact and operational for five years. The scheme provided for inspections.

Micro enterprises had a separate generator component within HGUVY. Selecting the enterprise classification is therefore necessary before choosing the notification.

sections.title: Before assessing a purchase
sections.html:
Keep the capacity specification, fuel type, invoice, supplier details, bank payment and installation evidence together. Match the applicant and installation address with Udyam, HUM and land records. Establish the purchase and commercial-production dates and retrieve any earlier application acknowledgement.

The original filing trigger was linked to purchase, with a three-month period in the notification. Current operating permissions for the actual generator are a separate matter: financial assistance does not authorise its use under pollution-control or air-quality restrictions.

Does this page establish that a new diesel generator can receive assistance today?

No. It explains the historic notified scheme. A present purchase needs the operative policy, applicable emissions restrictions and project dates assessed before an incentive is included in the budget.

title: Testing Equipment Assistance in Haryana
h1: Testing Equipment Assistance in Haryana
description: How Haryana’s testing-equipment assistance relates to quality-control investment, eligible purchases and evidence for a claim.
metaTitle: Haryana Testing Equipment Assistance: HEEP 2020 | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s 2021 Testing Equipment Assistance Scheme supported equipment used to check raw materials or finished products. For a manufacturer, the practical value is stronger control over product quality through an in-house testing capability. The equipment’s testing function matters more than a supplier describing it as a “quality machine”.

The Haryana Testing Equipment Assistance Scheme notified on 8 June 2021 provided support for qualifying MSMEs. It should be distinguished from reimbursement of an external laboratory’s test charges and from assistance for obtaining a quality certificate.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: What the notified assistance covered
sections.html:
The 2021 scheme provided 50% support for the purchase of testing equipment, subject to a maximum of ₹20 lakh per year. It excluded second-hand testing equipment. The unit had to be in commercial production, meet the scheme’s registration and other eligibility conditions, and remain in regular production at disbursement.

The purchased equipment was to be retained for five years without disposal unless the competent authority approved it. This makes the asset register and continuing physical availability important after the initial claim, not just at purchase.

sections.title: Explain the measurement the equipment performs
sections.html:
A strong file identifies the raw material or product being tested, the property measured, the relevant production stage and the equipment’s technical specification. If one machine performs both production and testing tasks, describe those functions clearly instead of assuming the full price has the same treatment.

Keep the purchase order, invoice, payment evidence, installation records and equipment identification together. Technical brochures help explain the function; they do not replace purchase and payment evidence. Udyam and HUM details, applicable approvals and commercial-production records should agree with the applicant and site shown in the claim.

The original scheme required a complete claim within three months of purchase or notification, whichever was later. Its specified purchase period and any later extensions must be read alongside the 2026 policy transition. An existing claim should retain its original submission acknowledgement and all subsequent correspondence.

sections.title: Claim process
sections.html:
The notified route was an online application to the Directorate of MSME, followed by District MSME Centre scrutiny and inspection. The inspection connects the documents to the actual equipment at the unit. Clarifications should answer the particular technical or cost issue raised, with consistent invoices and records.

Does a production machine qualify because it improves quality?

Improving quality is not enough by itself. The application needs to establish that the proposed asset is testing equipment within the applicable scheme.

Is a quality certificate part of the same claim?

A certificate and a testing asset are different expenditure heads. See Quality Certification Assistance for the separate topic and assess any overlap in funding before claiming.

title: Electricity Duty Exemption in Haryana
h1: Electricity Duty Exemption in Haryana
description: Electricity duty exemption affects a specific bill component. Understand Haryana’s historic categories, evidence and policy transition.
metaTitle: Electricity Duty Exemption Haryana: HEEP 2020 | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Under Haryana’s HEEP 2020 notification, electricity duty exemption reduced or removed the electricity-duty component for an eligible enterprise. It does not mean free electricity, and it does not by itself remove energy charges, demand charges or other items on a power bill.

Haryana’s June 2021 HEEP notification provided different exemption periods for enterprise and sector categories. The practical starting point is to identify the applicable category, the site’s block and the date from which the exemption could run.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: Why one exemption period does not fit every unit
sections.html:
The notification distinguished MSMEs, large and mega projects, thrust sectors, specified services and other categories. For example, ordinary manufacturing MSMEs had a different period from the listed service enterprises. A firm’s size or Udyam registration alone did not establish which line of the notification applied.

An exemption also needs the correct electricity connection. The meter, consumer account, enterprise name and industrial site should align with the application. If an expansion uses an existing connection, establish what investment and consumption the approval actually covers.

sections.title: Prepare the consumption and project record
sections.html:
Collect the electricity bill and connection details, commercial-production evidence, applicable registration records, block identification and relevant project approvals. Bills should show the duty charged separately so that the claimed treatment can be checked. Preserve any earlier exemption order and the period it specifies.

For a running unit, reconcile the order with subsequent bills and raise a supported query where the treatment differs. For a new project, first establish which current notification applies and the authority’s application requirements. Do not assume an old approval for another unit transfers with a property or power connection.

Is electricity duty the same as the power tariff?

No. Tariff and duty are distinct bill components. A tariff assistance scheme and duty exemption must be assessed and recorded separately.

Does every B, C or D block project get the same benefit?

No. The historic notification also used enterprise and sector categories. The applicable classification and dates must be proved.

title: Haryana Investment Subsidy in Lieu of Net SGST
h1: Haryana Investment Subsidy in Lieu of Net SGST
description: Understand the historic HEEP net SGST incentive, eligible tax payments and the records required to assess a Haryana claim.
metaTitle: Haryana Net SGST Subsidy: HEEP 2020 Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml: The historic HEEP 2020 investment subsidy used eligible net SGST paid by a qualifying enterprise as the basis for assistance. Its value depends on the unit’s category, block location, investment and actual tax payment. A business with a large turnover can still have a much smaller eligible cash-ledger payment after input tax credit.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: Establish the right category first
sections.html:
The July 2021 notification contains different provisions for MSMEs, large and mega projects, specified sectors, services and other defined categories. It also addresses qualifying expansion and diversification. The rate, benefit period and fixed-capital-investment ceiling must all come from the same applicable category.

An expansion assessment needs the existing investment base and the additional plant and machinery separately identified. A new company name or GST registration alone does not prove that an existing operation is a qualifying new investment.

sections.title: Work from the cash ledger
sections.html:
The notified net SGST definition concerns cash-ledger payment against SGST output liability on eligible products, after using eligible input tax credit, including applicable IGST credit. The claim therefore needs a reconciliation from returns and credit utilisation to cash payment and the eligible unit’s activity.

Prepare a year-by-year schedule showing the eligible tax amount, applicable subsidy share, amount already claimed and the remaining investment ceiling. This makes both the annual calculation and cumulative benefit visible. Where several units share a registration, the attribution method needs specific examination before a figure is presented.

sections.title: Claim preparation
sections.html:
The core records are the unit’s constitution and registrations, location, production date, investment invoices and payments, fixed-asset schedule, GST returns and ledgers. Preserve earlier eligibility orders, claim decisions and departmental correspondence for a continuing claim.

The filing route and period should be checked against the notification governing that unit and any transition instructions. A general policy summary cannot establish the admissibility of a particular tax year.

Read the July 2021 HEEP SGST notification and 2026 successor policy. The textile SGST scheme and EV SGST scheme are separately documented policy routes. Their rates and years should not be substituted into a HEEP claim.

title: Fire Equipment and Safety Compliance Assistance
h1: Fire Equipment and Safety Compliance Assistance
description: Understand the Haryana Safety Compliance Scheme behind fire-equipment subsidy enquiries, including audit, investment and evidence requirements.
metaTitle: Haryana Safety Compliance & Fire Equipment Assistance | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
A fire-equipment subsidy enquiry should begin with the safety work being carried out and the scheme that covers it. Haryana’s 8 June 2021 Safety Compliance Scheme supported safety audits and qualifying capital equipment or expenditure for safety measures. The official title is broader than “Fire Equipment Subsidy”.

Buying an extinguisher, installing a fire system and completing a safety audit are different actions. A scheme claim needs to explain the expenditure and how it meets the applicable notification. It also needs to remain separate from obtaining a fire approval or maintaining required safety arrangements.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: The benefit had two parts
sections.html:
Under the 2021 notification, safety-audit reimbursement was 75% of eligible expense, capped at ₹1 lakh. Assistance for qualifying safety capital equipment and expenditure was 50%, subject to different caps for A, B, C and D blocks, once in five years. The capital ceiling therefore cannot be stated correctly without the unit’s block category.

The notification linked the safety-audit benefit to implementation of the audit recommendations. It specified an audit by auditors of an ISO-certified agency, new safety investment and an operating MSME that met the registration and applicable approval conditions. An audit report left without action did not meet the stated basis for audit assistance.

sections.title: Prepare the audit-to-investment record
sections.html:
The useful starting point is the audit report and its recommendations. Link each claimed item to the safety issue it addresses, then show the approved specification, invoice, payment and installation. Record which recommendations have been completed and which remain outstanding.

For a fire-safety system, equipment descriptions should identify the actual installation, not only a bundled supplier amount. Civil work, equipment and professional services may need separate treatment. The safety professional’s design and implementation records provide context for the claim; government incentive approval does not certify that the facility is safe.

The original notification required a complete claim within three months of the relevant audit or equipment event, or notification, whichever was later. Project chronology and any earlier submission therefore matter. District scrutiny and site inspection form part of the notified process.

sections.title: Questions owners ask
sections.html:
Does a fire NOC create subsidy eligibility?

No. A fire approval and financial assistance have different requirements. The approval may be relevant evidence, but it does not replace the scheme’s applicant, activity and expense conditions.

Can I claim all fire-system costs under one percentage?

The eligible expenditure and block-based cap must be established first. A quotation total is not automatically the accepted cost base.

sections.title: Official sources and related support
sections.html: Read the Safety Compliance Scheme notification and the July 2026 policy notification. For the approval work itself, see Approvals & Compliance.

sections.title: See the work in a project context
sections.html: Our Hisar safety-equipment case describes subsidy-related application work around approximately ₹30 lakh in recorded new safety-equipment expenditure. The figure describes the investment, not a subsidy amount, and the case retains its evidence note. It is an example of the work, not confirmation that a new project qualifies.

sections.title: Discuss your safety-investment requirement
sections.html:
Tell us where the unit is located, which safety work is proposed or completed, its approximate cost and the main audit, purchase and installation dates. If a claim has already been filed, mention its current stage.

title: Stamp Duty Reimbursement in Haryana
h1: Stamp Duty Reimbursement in Haryana
description: Haryana industrial stamp-duty support depends on the land transaction, project category and production dates. Prepare the right evidence.
metaTitle: Stamp Duty Reimbursement Haryana: HEEP 2020 | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s HEEP 2020 stamp-duty reimbursement concerned duty paid on a qualifying land transaction for the enterprise. Its value depends on the applicable policy and the actual stamp duty paid, not on the entire purchase price of the property.

The June 2021 Haryana Stamp Duty Refund Scheme under HEEP 2020 differentiated block and enterprise categories and linked several benefits to commencement of commercial production within five years of the land purchase. Buying industrial land did not complete the claim conditions on its own.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: Connect the land to the operating project
sections.html:
For a claim, the sale deed, stamp-duty payment and land particulars need to connect to the enterprise and the project for which support is sought. Check the purchaser’s legal identity, the property’s permitted use and the date the qualifying business began production.

The original notification provided different percentages for categories including general MSMEs, thrust sectors and other specified enterprises. A rate quoted for one category should not be used for a different business. Lease-related or sector-policy assistance also needs its own source rather than being inferred from a land-purchase provision.

sections.title: Records to preserve
sections.html:
Keep the registered instrument, duty-payment receipt, ownership history, project registrations, land-use records, commercial-production evidence and earlier incentive approvals together. If a business is expanding, show which land and investment relate to the expansion. Where another entity bought the property, assess the legal relationship before assuming the operating company can claim the duty.

Prepare the claim against the applicable notification and submit through the prescribed departmental process. Retain the application acknowledgement and any deficiencies or orders. An amount should remain a claim under consideration until the authority has actually sanctioned or disbursed it.

Can I deduct the anticipated reimbursement from the amount payable at registration?

A reimbursement claim does not itself authorise paying less at registration. Any upfront exemption needs its own legal basis and required approval.

Is land-use permission covered by the reimbursement?

No. Stamp-duty support and permission to use land are separate. See Approvals & Compliance for the project’s approval requirements.

title: CGTMSE Fee Reimbursement in Haryana
h1: CGTMSE Fee Reimbursement in Haryana
description: Understand Haryana’s CGTMSE guarantee-fee reimbursement, how it differs from a bank fee refund, and which records an existing claim needs.
metaTitle: CGTMSE Fee Refund in Haryana: Reimbursement Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
CGTMSE fees are not automatically refundable when a business repays its loan. The Haryana scheme commonly described as the “CGTMSE fee refund” is a state reimbursement provision, officially notified as the Collateral Free Credit Guarantee Scheme under HEEP 2020. It concerned eligible micro enterprises in Haryana and the guarantee-cover fee charged by their financial institution or bank.

That distinction answers the first practical question: a state incentive claim, a bank’s correction of a wrong charge and CGTMSE’s own fee rules are different matters. A loan account showing a guarantee fee does not, by itself, establish a right to reimbursement.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: What the 2021 notification provided
sections.html:
The notification provided reimbursement of 100% of the guarantee-cover fee charged for qualifying collateral-free term loans or working-capital facilities under CGTMSE, for five years. The borrowing unit had to meet the scheme’s micro-enterprise conditions, be in commercial production and remain in regular production when assistance was disbursed. It also required Udyam registration, Haryana Udhyam Memorandum and applicable land-use or other approvals.

The benefit was tied to a specific fee. It was not a refund of the loan principal, all interest paid or every bank charge. Processing fees, insurance premiums and other debits should be identified separately before the claim amount is prepared. The notified lender and credit-facility conditions also need to be checked against the actual sanction.

sections.title: Build the claim around bank evidence
sections.html:
Start with the sanction letter and a bank confirmation identifying the CGTMSE-covered facility. Reconcile the guarantee fee charged, the period it relates to and the amount actually paid with the account statement. A generic bank statement description may need clarification from the branch.

Keep the enterprise registrations, commercial-production evidence, earlier claim acknowledgements and any sanction or deficiency correspondence together. The 2021 notification contained a three-month claim deadline linked to commencement of operations or notification, whichever was later. An existing file needs its own deadline and subsequent orders checked; a newly dated invoice does not necessarily reopen an expired claim period.

The notified process routes the claim through the Haryana department’s portal and District MSME Centre examination. The bank supplies credit and fee evidence; the department decides the incentive claim.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.html:
Does closing the loan make the fee refundable?

Closing a loan does not itself prove a reimbursement entitlement. First establish which fee was charged, which rules applied and whether a state claim was made within the relevant conditions.

Is this available to every MSME?

The cited Haryana notification specifically addressed micro enterprises. “MSME” in a loan advertisement is broader and should not be substituted for that condition.

sections.title: Official reference
sections.html: Read the Haryana Collateral Free Credit Guarantee Scheme notification and the July 2026 policy notification together when assessing the policy transition.

sections.title: Discuss your guarantee-fee claim
sections.html:

Keep bank statements and correspondence available for the assessment; you do not need to upload them to make the first enquiry.

title: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund
h1: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund
description: Understand AHIDF’s eligible infrastructure, lending conditions and the distinction between approval and disbursement periods.
metaTitle: AHIDF: Eligibility, Approval & Disbursement Periods | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) supports qualifying investment in dairy, meat, animal feed and other specified animal-husbandry infrastructure through a lending and interest-support framework. It is relevant to processing and value addition as well as the other activities expressly identified in the programme.

The Department’s Operational Guidelines 3.0 reflect AHIDF’s continuation with the Dairy Processing Infrastructure Development Fund incorporated into it. Older FAQs that exclude dairy cooperatives do not describe the full revised applicant scope.

sections.title: Approval dates and disbursement dates differ
sections.html:
The revised framework states an approval-period endpoint of 31 March 2026. Clause 12.1 allows lenders to disburse for sanctioned projects approved on or before that date, but not beyond 31 March 2027. That later date is a disbursement provision for qualifying approved projects, not evidence of a fresh application window.

The longer programme sunset and repayment periods also serve different purposes. A new applicant needs any subsequent approval authority established before treating AHIDF as available for the proposal. An already approved borrower should check the remaining disbursement conditions and deadline with the lender.

sections.title: Which projects and applicants fit?
sections.html:
The revised framework identifies dairy and meat processing, animal-feed plants, specified breed-improvement and multiplication activities, veterinary vaccine and drug manufacturing, animal-waste-to-wealth management and primary wool processing. Each category has a defined activity scope. Owning livestock or handling an animal-origin product does not by itself establish eligibility.

Permitted applicant categories include individual entrepreneurs, private companies, MSMEs, FPOs, Section 8 companies and dairy cooperatives, subject to the relevant activity and lending conditions. Establish the applicant, asset and business process together.

sections.title: What financial support means in practice
sections.html:
The guideline permits loans up to 90% of eligible project cost, based on a viable project and the lender’s assessment. Beneficiary contribution varies by enterprise category and financing requirements. The maximum loan share is not a promise that every applicant can contribute only 10%.

Interest assistance follows the applicable programme and sanction terms. The revised document preserves distinctions between earlier AHIDF and DIDF projects, so their historical rates should not be applied indiscriminately to another borrower.

The guideline excludes interest support on borrowing for specified costs, including land, working capital, pre-operative expenditure, existing infrastructure acquisition, old machinery and personal-use vehicles. It also links support to loan performance. Prepare the eligible borrowing schedule separately from the total project and monitor how support is credited to the loan account.

sections.title: Prepare a project and claim file that agree
sections.html:
The project report should connect raw-material supply, process capacity, product demand, machinery, utilities and financial projections. Assemble applicant and ownership records, land arrangements, technical quotations, permissions, the loan appraisal and financing commitments.

For an approved project, retain the original sanction, programme approval, disbursements, actual expenditure, completion and repayment records. A request to the lender should identify whether the issue concerns disbursement, interest-support credit or a project change. These are different stages with different evidence.

Read the AHIDF Operational Guidelines 3.0 and the Department’s programme overview. For a separate processing grant, assess CEFPPC on its own rules and non-duplication conditions.

title: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
h1: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
description: AIF supports eligible agriculture infrastructure through loan interest assistance. Understand project scope, financing conditions and preparation.
metaTitle: AIF Scheme: Eligibility, Interest Support & Loan Period | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund helps finance eligible agricultural infrastructure through interest support on loans. It can be relevant to a warehouse, cold store, sorting and grading facility or qualifying processing project where the activity fits the scheme’s defined agricultural value chain.

AIF is a financing facility. Its value to a project lies in reducing the interest burden on qualifying borrowing and supporting access to credit guarantees. It does not turn the full cost of a facility into a capital grant, and the lender still assesses whether the business can repay the loan.

sections.title: Assistance and policy period
sections.html:
The September 2024 revised guidelines provide 3% annual interest subvention on eligible borrowing up to ₹2 crore, for a maximum of seven years. A larger loan can be considered, but that guideline limits the interest-supported portion to ₹2 crore. Credit-guarantee support is subject to the eligible borrower and guarantee framework.

The document gives the scheme an overall period through 2032–33, while setting the loan-disbursement period through 2025–26. These dates serve different purposes. The longer support period does not establish that new loan applications remain open after March 2026. A new proposal needs the latest disbursement authority and lender instructions checked before AIF is included in its financing plan.

sections.title: Which activity is being financed?
sections.html:
The revised list includes warehouses and silos, cold stores and cold-chain facilities, assaying, packaging, sorting, grading and specified logistics infrastructure. It also covers defined farming assets and certain farm-residue or waste-management activities. Each description has its own conditions; an agricultural connection in the business name is insufficient.

The 2024 revision distinguishes eligible primary processing and integrated primary-plus-secondary processing from standalone secondary processing, which is excluded. For example, a proposal must explain how the actual processing stages fit the crop-wise activity table. It is not enough to describe the entire investment simply as “food processing”.

Applicant categories include farmers, agri-entrepreneurs, start-ups, farmer producer organisations and other bodies identified in the guidelines. Some activities carry applicant-specific restrictions. Establish the applicant, asset, location and operating model together.

sections.title: Prepare a financeable project
sections.html:
A useful project file links the proposed asset to the produce it will handle, the capacity required and the income expected. For a warehouse, that means examining throughput, occupancy, storage charges and operating costs. For a processing line, it means showing the input, process stages, output and market.

Keep land or lease records, technical quotations, a cost breakdown, project report and proposed means of finance ready. Separate land, civil works, equipment and working capital. The bank needs repayment evidence and the scheme assessment needs eligible-activity evidence; the two reviews answer related but different questions.

Confirm the operative application route, submit the proposal and lender documentation, respond to appraisal queries, and preserve sanction and disbursement records. Interest support must be reconciled with the actual loan account over time.

sections.title: Common questions
sections.html:
Is every warehouse eligible?

No. The proposed use must fit AIF’s agricultural infrastructure scope. A general commercial storage building cannot be assumed to qualify simply because it is called a warehouse.

Can AIF be combined with another subsidy?

The guidelines provide for convergence, but the other programme’s conditions, eligible costs and financing treatment must also permit it. Prepare a component-level funding plan before counting both benefits.

sections.title: Official source
sections.html:
September 2024 revised AIF guidelines, particularly the implementation period, budgetary support and eligible-project sections.

For a different kind of warehouse assistance, read the separate explanations of Haryana warehouse capital assistance and AMI.

sections.html:

title: Interest Subsidy for Textile Units
h1: Interest Subsidy for Textile Units
description: Haryana textile interest assistance varies by activity, block and borrowing. Understand term-loan evidence and the policy extension.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Interest Subsidy: Loan & Claim Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s textile Interest Subsidy Scheme addresses the cost of qualifying term loans for new projects, expansion, diversification and modernisation. It is relevant to the financing of the investment, so the bank sanction and interest actually paid are central to the assessment.

The scheme was notified on 5 July 2023 under the Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy. The May 2025 amendment extended the policy and its related schemes to 18 December 2026. That extension does not establish an applicant’s remaining support period or confirm that a particular claim can still be filed.

sections.title: Match the loan to the textile activity
sections.html:
The notification sets separate arrangements for textile MSMEs and textile-machinery manufacturing MSMEs. For textile MSMEs, it specifies 6% interest support with a ₹20 lakh annual ceiling in B blocks, and 7% with respective annual ceilings of ₹30 lakh and ₹50 lakh in C and D blocks, for seven years. The machinery-manufacturing category has different limits.

A loan for unrelated expenditure should not be added to the claim merely because the borrower is a textile company. The project needs to satisfy the scheme’s new-investment or expansion definition and its eligible term-loan and production conditions.

sections.title: Show the investment and borrowing chronology
sections.html:
Prepare the bank sanction, drawdown schedule, interest certificate, repayment statement and the machinery or project schedule financed by the loan. Existing businesses should establish the fixed-investment baseline against which the expansion is being assessed. Identify sanction, disbursement, completion and commercial-production dates separately.

The scheme’s definition of expansion refers to more than 25% additional investment against existing gross fixed capital and completion within the stipulated period. This needs a defensible accounting and project record rather than a new label for ordinary expenditure.

For annual claims, reconcile the lender’s interest certificate with the books and loan statement. Separate penal interest, arrears or unrelated charges for review instead of applying the rate to all bank debits.

Can I receive both textile capital and interest assistance?

The provisions for each benefit and their interaction must be assessed against the same cost and financing schedule. Read Textile Capital Investment Subsidy as a separate component, not an automatic additional receipt.

title: ATUFS: Textile Machinery Support and Legacy Claims
h1: ATUFS: Textile Machinery Support and Legacy Claims
description: Understand ATUFS as a historic textile technology-upgradation programme and prepare the machinery evidence for an existing claim.
metaTitle: ATUFS: Textile Machinery Support and Legacy Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Amended Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme, or ATUFS, supported investment in eligible textile machinery through its notified capital-investment subsidy framework. Its implementation period ran from 13 January 2016 to 31 March 2022.

For a business reviewing ATUFS today, the useful question is usually the position of an earlier eligible investment or claim. An older scheme document or continuing subsidy payment does not establish that a newly purchased machine can enter ATUFS.

sections.title: Identify the original claim before recalculating it
sections.html:
Begin with the unit’s Unique Identification Number, loan sanction, machinery schedule and the version of the guideline applicable to that investment. ATUFS followed earlier versions of TUFS, each with its own rules. A bank account described broadly as “TUFS” needs its actual programme and sanction history identified.

The textile segment, eligible technology and approved machinery determine the assistance assessment. A general statement that modern machinery qualifies cannot replace the scheme’s machinery specifications and timing conditions.

sections.title: Machinery identity is material evidence
sections.html:
The Ministry’s amendments address serial numbers on machinery and their connection to invoices and import or shipping records. Joint inspection verifies installation and commissioning against the claim. Keep the original invoice, machine identification, payment and loan records together, and record any replacement or change in the installed assets.

Where records are incomplete, identify the precise gap and the permitted documentary remedy. An unsupported replacement invoice or a reconstructed purchase date can undermine the claim rather than resolve it.

sections.title: Establish the pending stage
sections.html:
A useful status review distinguishes UID registration, installation intimation, an inspection request, inspection findings, subsidy recommendation and release. Preserve deficiency notices and replies, because the applicable procedure may give a specific remedy or deadline at that stage.

Prepare a dated claim chronology with the amount sanctioned, recommended, released and still disputed or pending. That produces a concrete follow-up request for the lender or responsible authority without promising a release date.

Read the Ministry of Textiles ATUFS amendments. A new Haryana textile investment should separately assess state capital assistance and state interest assistance, including their current policy period and conditions.

title: Capital Investment Subsidy for Textile Units
h1: Capital Investment Subsidy for Textile Units
description: Haryana textile capital assistance: project categories, eligible investment, the December 2026 policy extension and application preparation.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Capital Subsidy: Investment & Eligibility | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s Capital Investment Subsidy for Textile Units supports qualifying investment across the textile value chain. The applicable benefit depends on what the unit manufactures, its block location and whether the investment is a new project, expansion, diversification or modernisation.

The scheme notified on 5 July 2023 under the Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy has a later amendment that matters to investment planning. The 2 May 2025 notification extends the policy and its schemes to 18 December 2026. It also removes the capital-subsidy limit on the number of cases, subject to the overall approved budget. An operative policy period is not confirmation that budget remains available for a particular application.

sections.title: Identify the correct investment category
sections.html:
The 2023 scheme separates general textile units, technical textiles and specified import-substitution or backward-integration projects, open-end spinning and waste-to-fibre units, and textile machinery manufacturers. Anchor units have a further category with different conditions. A project should be classified on its product, process and qualifying investment before choosing an assistance rate.

For general textile enterprises, the notified capital support is 30% of eligible investment, capped at ₹2.5 crore in B blocks, and 35%, capped at ₹3.5 crore in C and D blocks. Other categories have different limits. These figures describe that category under the cited scheme; they are not a single rate for every textile project.

The notification also contains category-specific enhancements and eligibility rules. Claiming a higher category needs evidence of the actual activity or qualifying ownership, not merely wording added to the project report.

sections.title: What is eligible capital investment?
sections.html:
The notification defines the cost base rather than using the project’s total headline value. Relevant investment may include specified plant and machinery, factory buildings, laboratories and utilities. It excludes items such as land, land development, working capital and listed preliminary or general civil expenditure.

For an expansion, the scheme definition refers to investment exceeding 25% of the existing gross fixed capital investment and completion within the stated period. Establish the existing investment baseline and the new project scope before preparing the calculation. Routine replacement purchases should not be labelled as a qualifying expansion without that assessment.

sections.title: Prepare the evidence before submission
sections.html:
Prepare a process description, itemised fixed-capital schedule, quotations and invoices, proof of payment, ownership and site records, commercial-production dates and the existing investment baseline where relevant. Match the project category to the technical evidence. For waste-to-fibre or technical textiles, explain what the finished material is and how it is produced.

The complete source pack should include the 2023 scheme, the 2025 amendments and the relevant implementation memorandum. Check the applicable application trigger, current portal process, budget position and restrictions on claiming other assistance on the same expenditure. Preserve inspection, sanction and disbursement records separately.

Is Haryana textile support the same as ATUFS?

No. ATUFS is a separate central programme with its own historic implementation period and claim records. A Haryana application cannot be assessed by copying an ATUFS rate.

Does the extension guarantee acceptance until December 2026?

No. It extends the operative period. Eligibility, application timing, budget and approval still need to be established for the project.

title: Haryana Textile Park Scheme
h1: Haryana Textile Park Scheme
description: Understand Haryana textile park support for developers, common infrastructure and qualifying textile investment.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Park Scheme: Developer & Facility Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s Textile Park Scheme supports the development of a location where multiple textile manufacturers can operate with planned infrastructure. The applicant’s role is the park promoter or developer. An individual textile factory has a different subsidy assessment, even when it will occupy land in the park.

The July 2023 scheme sits under the Haryana AatmaNirbhar Textile Policy. A May 2025 notification extended that policy and its schemes to 18 December 2026. This policy period does not, by itself, confirm approval capacity or an open submission facility for every park proposal.

sections.title: What makes a qualifying park?
sections.html:
The notified model requires at least 20 acres in a B, C or D category block, at least 10 manufacturing units and the prescribed aggregate fixed-capital investment of ₹30 crore. Location, the participant mix and the nature of manufacturing therefore matter before detailed infrastructure costs are prepared.

The developer should establish a coherent layout: industrial plots or premises, access, power, water, drainage and treatment facilities must serve the proposed occupiers. Land ownership and permissions need to support the intended development and use.

sections.title: What support does the notification describe?
sections.html:
The scheme provides specified relief on stamp duty and internal development charges, together with support for a qualifying common zero-liquid-discharge facility. The latter is a contribution towards eligible facility cost, with land excluded; it is not a subsidy on all land and construction expenditure in the park.

The July 2023 notification sets out 50% assistance for the common ZLD facility, capped at ₹10 crore. Its technical scope, common use and approved expenditure must be established. The developer should keep this cost schedule separate from infrastructure sold or leased with individual plots.

sections.title: Evidence and implementation
sections.html:
Prepare the title or tenure documents, block classification, master plan, participating-unit details and their proposed investment. Treatment-facility design should connect to the effluent quantity and characteristics of the proposed industries, along with the approvals needed for operation.

The application and sanction must identify who creates, owns and maintains the common assets. A development business case should also explain how maintenance and treatment costs will be recovered from occupiers. Approval of an incentive does not replace planning or environmental permissions.

Read the Textile Park Scheme and the May 2025 policy extension. For a common facility led by a group of existing textile MSMEs, see Textile Cluster Development. For the factory’s own investment, see Textile Capital Investment Subsidy.

title: Haryana Textile Cluster Development Scheme
h1: Haryana Textile Cluster Development Scheme
description: Explore common facilities for a group of textile MSMEs, including SPV ownership, contribution and project preparation.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Cluster Scheme: Common Facility Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Textile businesses can share equipment and services that would be difficult for each unit to finance and operate alone. Haryana’s Textile Cluster Development Scheme provides a route for a qualifying group of textile MSMEs to establish a common facility centre.

The scheme is collective: the member units use the facility, while a dedicated organisation develops and operates it. Buying a machine for one member’s factory does not become a cluster project simply because other businesses support the application.

sections.title: Membership and ownership
sections.html:
The July 2023 notification requires a group of at least 15 textile MSMEs within the prescribed 50-kilometre area, which may extend across Haryana districts. The special purpose vehicle, or SPV, must be constituted as a Section 8 not-for-profit company under the scheme.

This legal form matters. Member contributions, ownership of assets, access to facilities and continuing management should sit within that entity’s approved arrangements. The member list should identify operating units, products, addresses and the need each member has for the proposed common service.

sections.title: Assistance follows an approved common need
sections.html:
The scheme provides for 90% state contribution and 10% SPV contribution for an eligible common-facility project costing up to ₹10 crore. Upgradation of an existing common facility may also be considered within the notified conditions. These figures apply to the approved project, not to every expenditure proposed by the members.

Start with a diagnostic assessment of the cluster. It should explain the shared constraint, expected users, required capacity and how the facility will improve the members’ operations. Testing, processing or other equipment should be selected against this need, supported by technical specifications and costs.

sections.title: Build the operating model before the application
sections.html:
The SPV needs to demonstrate land arrangements, member contribution, management capability and a plan to keep the facility running. User charges, staffing, maintenance, utilities and replacement costs should be addressed in the project report. A common facility that cannot recover operating costs can become a liability for its members.

The notification includes a requirement to make the centre functional within two years of final approval. Procurement, construction and permissions therefore need a workable sequence. Keep member resolutions, payments, procurement records and progress evidence aligned with the sanctioned project.

The textile policy and its schemes were extended to 18 December 2026. Verify the current application process and project availability separately. Read the Textile Cluster Development notification and policy extension. The wider MSE Cluster Development Programme and Haryana Mini Cluster scheme have their own rules and should not be mixed into this calculation.

title: Warehousing Capital Subsidy in Haryana
h1: Warehousing Capital Subsidy in Haryana
description: Haryana warehouse capital assistance is distinct from AIF and AMI. Understand the 2019 policy’s project definitions, eligible cost and claim evidence.
metaTitle: Warehouse Capital Subsidy Haryana: 2019 Policy | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s warehouse capital assistance was notified under the Logistics, Warehousing & Retail Policy, 2019. It addressed qualifying fixed investment in warehousing projects in C and D blocks. It is a separate state-policy benefit from AIF loan interest support and AMI agricultural marketing assistance.

The 2019 scheme had a five-year operating provision unless superseded. This page explains that notified framework for readers assessing an older investment or claim. Fresh entitlement, any extension and later-policy treatment must be established before it is relied on for a new project.

sections.title: A warehouse is not automatically a logistics park
sections.html:
The notification defined warehouses, logistics parks and integrated or multi-modal logistics parks separately. Each has its own facility requirements. A standalone storage building should not be assigned a logistics-park ceiling simply because vehicles use the site.

For warehouses, the capital-assistance provision was 25% of eligible fixed capital investment, capped at ₹5 crore. Separate ceilings applied to logistics parks and multi-modal parks. The warehouse provision required the relevant C or D block location and continuing commercial operation for ten years; failure to meet that continuing condition could lead to recovery.

sections.title: What the capital calculation included
sections.html:
The notified eligible base concerned new building, machinery and equipment investment made before commencement of commercial operations. Land cost should not be folded into that base merely because the accountant’s overall fixed-asset schedule includes it.

The source also prescribed facility and access requirements and an additional-investment test for existing enterprises. Those historic scheme definitions should be checked alongside the current land and building rules for the particular site. A subsidy application does not replace development permission.

sections.title: Build a project-specific claim file
sections.html:
Start with the storage use, site plan, land documents, permitted activity, facility capacity and actual commencement date. Add the certified fixed-investment schedule, itemised building and equipment details, invoices, payment evidence and audited accounts where relevant. An existing enterprise should show its original investment and expansion separately.

The capital provision called for a claim within three months of commencement of commercial services, operations or production. For a legacy file, preserve that first submission and subsequent departmental orders. An operating warehouse with no timely claim is a different case from an already sanctioned project awaiting release.

Does every grain godown qualify for all three warehouse schemes?

No. Haryana capital support, AMI and AIF use different cost bases, financing structures and activity conditions. Compare each against the actual facility and check any restrictions on combined support.

title: CEFPPC: Food Processing and Preservation Capacity Support
h1: CEFPPC: Food Processing and Preservation Capacity Support
description: Understand CEFPPC project costs, funding conditions and application preparation under MoFPI’s January 2025 guidelines.
metaTitle: CEFPPC Scheme: Eligibility, Costs & Application Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Creation/Expansion of Food Processing and Preservation Capacities (CEFPPC) scheme supports the creation or expansion of food processing and preservation capacity through a grant towards eligible project expenditure. It can make a meaningful difference to a processing investment, but the grant calculation starts with the approved equipment and technical civil work, not the total amount you plan to spend.

The Ministry of Food Processing Industries issued revised guidelines on 22 January 2025. Applications are invited through an Expression of Interest, or EOI. A published guideline does not itself open applications, and the 2025 invitation should not be treated as a current application window.

sections.title: What kind of project fits?
sections.html:
The scheme covers specified food-processing activities, including food grains, dairy, meat, fish, fruit and vegetables, edible oils, spices and ready-to-eat products. The proposal must create processing or preservation capacity, or demonstrate the required increase in an existing operation. A standalone storage or transport business does not qualify merely because it handles food.

Individuals and several forms of business or producer organisation can apply within the notified conditions. Projects may be located inside or outside a recognised food park or agro-processing cluster. The product, process and applicant category must still match the guideline. Farming expenditure and a general warehouse cannot be folded into a processing proposal to make them eligible.

sections.title: How the grant is calculated
sections.html:
The January 2025 guideline provides assistance at 35% of eligible project cost in general areas and 50% in difficult areas and for qualifying SC/ST, FPO and SHG projects, subject to a maximum grant of ₹5 crore. Category treatment has documentary requirements. For example, the SC/ST route requires at least 51% ownership and conditions on maintaining that stake.

Eligible cost includes approved plant and machinery, specified utilities and technical civil work. Land, general civil works, working capital, consultancy, taxes and second-hand equipment are among the excluded items. Applicable cost norms also constrain the assessed amount. An invoice in the project budget is therefore not automatically a grant-bearing cost.

Minimum eligible project cost is ₹3 crore for general-area proposals and ₹1 crore for the specified difficult-area and SC/ST proposals. Minimum project size, promoter contribution, net worth and term loan are separate tests. The relevant category should be checked against each test individually.

sections.title: Funding and purchase timing matter
sections.html:
General-area applicants ordinarily need term finance of at least 20% of total project cost and the prescribed promoter contribution. Specified categories have different thresholds. A bank’s appraisal note is required; a stamped project report alone is insufficient. The guideline also ties the eligible term-loan sanction date to the EOI.

Most critically, the 2025 rules exclude expenditure on eligible components incurred before the Ministry issues its approval letter. Ordering or paying for machinery early can therefore affect the claim even where the machinery itself is eligible. Bring the proposed purchasing schedule into the eligibility assessment before making commitments.

sections.title: Prepare a proposal that can be checked
sections.html:
The application should connect raw-material availability, processing capacity, machinery, utilities, sales assumptions and finance. Assemble the land title or qualifying lease, process flow, itemised quotations, technical civil estimates, net-worth evidence, ownership records, loan sanction and bank appraisal. An expansion needs a clear existing-versus-proposed capacity statement and evidence of the operating unit.

Submit through the prescribed SAMPADA process during an applicable EOI. Technical appraisal and selection determine approval; submission does not create an entitlement. After approval, maintain component-wise invoices, banking records, contribution evidence and implementation progress so that release requests can be reconciled with the sanctioned project. Grant release also remains subject to available funds.

Read the January 2025 CEFPPC guidelines. For shared infrastructure serving multiple processing businesses, compare the separate Agro-Processing Cluster scheme.

title: Haryana Food Processing Unit Assistance under the 2018 Policy
h1: Haryana Food Processing Unit Assistance under the 2018 Policy
description: Understand the historic Haryana food-processing unit route and the evidence needed to assess an earlier investment.
metaTitle: Haryana Food Processing Assistance: 2018 Policy | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s Agri-Business and Food Processing Policy 2018 included assistance for individual processing units in C and D category blocks. This state-policy route is distinct from MoFPI’s central CEFPPC scheme, even though both can appear in searches for food-processing unit assistance.

The June 2023 state amendment expressly addresses new, expansion and diversification units in those blocks, with the stated change effective from 19 October 2021. The location and investment history therefore matter when identifying an older project’s scheme basis.

sections.title: The policy version is part of the assessment
sections.html:
Haryana notified a new Agri-Business and Food Processing Policy on 29 May 2026, superseding the 2018 policy. The older unit-assistance provision should be used as a historical reference, with transition provisions and operative implementing instructions checked for the actual project.

The 2023 amendment alone does not provide the full unit-scheme cost definition, procedure or benefit calculation. A percentage taken from the central scheme or an unrelated state policy cannot fill that gap. An earlier sanction or complete implementing notification is needed before a dependable amount can be established.

sections.title: Define the investment being claimed
sections.html:
For a new unit, identify the product, process, site, machinery and production date. For an expansion or diversification, preserve the original capacity and assets alongside the additional investment. This makes it possible to distinguish a qualifying project from routine replacement or maintenance.

Prepare the location and block evidence, land documents, registrations, machinery invoices, technical civil costs, payments and financing. Connect each asset to the processing activity and keep excluded or unrelated expenditure separate pending the scheme-specific assessment.

sections.title: Reviewing a historic application
sections.html:
Bring the original application, acknowledgement, eligibility order, sanction and correspondence into one chronology. Record what was claimed, what was approved, what has been paid and the precise issue still outstanding. Those facts help establish the correct transition and procedural question.

Read the June 2023 state food-policy amendment and 2026 successor food policy. A proposed central application should be assessed through the separate CEFPPC entry.

title: Agro-Processing Cluster Infrastructure Scheme
h1: Agro-Processing Cluster Infrastructure Scheme
description: Assess common food-processing infrastructure, cluster scale and grant conditions under MoFPI’s April 2025 APC guidelines.
metaTitle: Agro-Processing Cluster Scheme: Eligibility & Grant Costs | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
An agro-processing cluster brings several food-processing units together around common infrastructure. Under MoFPI’s April 2025 guidelines, the grant supports that shared infrastructure. The factories established within the cluster have their own investments and operations.

This structure suits a developer or implementing agency able to assemble land, finance, infrastructure and participating businesses. It requires more than a proposal to build and rent a few industrial sheds.

sections.title: The cluster has to work as a whole
sections.html:
The guideline requires at least five food-processing units with aggregate investment of at least ₹25 crore. Investment in those units is separate from the eligible infrastructure cost used to calculate the cluster grant. The proposal must show how the units and common facilities will be established and used.

Ordinarily, the site needs at least 10 acres, held through ownership or a qualifying lease of at least 50 years. The guideline allows a smaller land threshold for specified urban arrangements involving vertical development. That exception requires examination of the actual location and layout; it is not a general five-acre rule.

Common infrastructure can include internal roads, drainage and utilities, alongside core facilities such as cold storage, packaging or testing. The selected facilities should answer the needs of the proposed units. A facility with no realistic user base can weaken both appraisal and the eventual operating business.

sections.title: Assistance and eligible cost
sections.html:
The April 2025 guideline provides 35% of eligible project cost in general areas and 50% in difficult areas and for qualifying SC/ST, FPO and SHG projects, subject to a maximum of ₹10 crore. Land is excluded. Basic enabling infrastructure is also limited within the eligible-cost structure, so the entire site-development bill cannot simply be multiplied by the grant rate.

Prepare separate schedules for land, basic infrastructure, core infrastructure and each processing unit. This makes the grant calculation, bank funding and responsibility for each asset visible. The guideline prescribes promoter contribution, term lending and net-worth requirements, with category-specific provisions.

sections.title: From proposal to an operating cluster
sections.html:
A useful application includes the land documents, master plan, infrastructure specifications, cost estimates, bank appraisal and credible commitments from proposed processing units. It should explain the product mix, common-facility capacity, water and power demand, waste handling and the agency responsible for operating and maintaining shared assets.

Applications are considered against an EOI and assessed on their merits. Approval fixes the eligible scope and grant; subsequent cost increases do not automatically increase assistance. The Ministry’s 2025 EOI had a defined closing date. Confirm a presently applicable invitation before treating a new proposal as ready for submission.

After approval, implementation and expenditure records must distinguish the common project from unit-level investment. That separation helps demonstrate the cluster conditions and avoids claiming the same component through two different projects.

See the April 2025 APC guidelines. A single processing unit should also consider whether its question belongs under CEFPPC.

title: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Scheme
h1: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure Scheme
description: Understand AMI’s credit-linked infrastructure model and the official June 2025 abeyance before planning a warehouse subsidy.
metaTitle: AMI Scheme: June 2025 Abeyance & Claim Context | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure scheme, or AMI, supports eligible agricultural storage and marketing infrastructure through a credit-linked subsidy route. The lender’s role is central: financing, project assessment and subsidy processing must connect to the same eligible project.

For a new investment, the present application position matters before any historical subsidy rate. NABARD’s Circular 149 placed implementation in abeyance with effect from 10 June 2025 because the available budget had been utilised. The circular suspended new sanctions and processing of pending subsidy claims until further orders and described the ENSURE portal as temporarily disabled for this purpose.

That is a dated official position. A later resumption has not been established for this explanation. Obtain the latest instructions from the financing bank and the implementing authorities before including AMI receipts in a project’s funding plan.

sections.title: What to assess in a storage project
sections.html:
The project’s purpose must fit agricultural marketing infrastructure. Establish the commodities, storage method, capacity, catchment and intended users. A building used for general commercial warehousing should not be assumed to qualify because it has the same floor area as an agricultural godown.

For a viable proposal, the capacity and specification should follow expected commodity flows. Land access, loading arrangements, handling losses, ventilation or temperature requirements, and fire and other permissions affect the project even before subsidy eligibility is considered.

sections.title: Keep the loan and subsidy calculations separate
sections.html:
The bank assesses whether it can finance the project and on what terms. Subsidy eligibility concerns the scheme’s applicant category, components, cost norms, dates and procedure. A term-loan sanction is not itself a subsidy approval, and a published subsidy rate does not oblige a lender to finance the investment.

Prepare the land records, layout, capacity calculation, itemised cost estimate, quotations, proposed utilisation and loan appraisal. For an existing project, add the sanction and disbursement dates, completion records, previous subsidy submissions and correspondence with the bank.

sections.title: If a claim is already pending
sections.html:
First establish its actual stage: submitted through the lender, acknowledged by the implementing system, sanctioned, inspected or awaiting release. The June 2025 circular affects processing; it does not justify inventing a new release date. The lender’s latest written position is more useful than treating all pending claims as identical.

Read NABARD Circular 149 on AMI abeyance. Compare Agriculture Infrastructure Fund only through its own eligibility and programme-period rules; it should not be treated as an automatic replacement grant.
