title: APEDA Financial Assistance for Agri-Food Exports
h1: APEDA Financial Assistance for Agri-Food Exports
description: Understand APEDA’s export infrastructure, quality and market-development support and the importance of approval timing.
metaTitle: APEDA Financial Assistance: 2021–26 Framework | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
APEDA’s Financial Assistance Scheme addresses specific gaps in agricultural and processed-food exports. Its 2021–26 framework groups assistance into export infrastructure, quality development and market development. The appropriate component follows the export problem the project will solve.

APEDA’s published scheme page identifies this Finance Commission cycle as 2021–22 to 2025–26. The 2024 focus-product invitation is also a dated notice. Confirm the operative programme and current invitation before relying on these terms for a new application.

sections.title: Choose the component that matches the expenditure
sections.html:
Export infrastructure can include specified pack-house facilities, grading and packing, pre-cooling and cold-chain facilities, treatment needed for destination-market requirements and identified processing gaps. Quality support addresses defined systems, testing and laboratory needs. Market development has its own eligible activities and participation conditions.

An applicant must also fit the relevant route, such as a registered exporter or another permitted organisation working with APEDA-scheduled products. Exporting food in general does not make every facility or marketing expense eligible.

sections.title: Approval timing affects admissibility
sections.html:
The 2021–26 guidelines distinguish expenditure incurred before online application from expenditure incurred afterwards. Spending after an application but before in-principle approval does not automatically qualify. Component-specific exceptions also exist, so a single purchasing rule should not be assumed to govern every claim.

Check the required approval and eligible-cost basis before placing orders. For equipment, the general conditions require competitive quotations and use the lowest qualifying quoted rate for assistance calculation. For civil work, the scope is technical civil work within the notified limits.

sections.title: Prepare an export-linked proposal
sections.html:
The application should connect the product, destination market, present constraint and proposed solution. Provide export and registration records, equipment specifications, quotations, technical civil estimates where applicable, ownership details and evidence of how the facility will be used.

After approval, retain the actual expenditure and payment records, approved scope, implementation evidence and required export-performance reporting. Assistance is released against completion and claim conditions; an application receipt is not a commitment to reimburse the full budget.

sections.title: Assess the amount component by component
sections.html:
Rates, ceilings and category provisions vary. Calculate each eligible activity separately, including exclusions and any other support. This is especially important where a proposal combines a pack house, laboratory and certification work, which may belong to different provisions.

Read the APEDA 2021–26 guidelines and official financial-assistance notices. For Haryana support connected specifically to outward shipment costs, see Freight Assistance.

description: Understand Haryana’s notified support for MSME boiler conversion to cleaner fuels and the distinction between compliance and subsidy.
metaTitle: Haryana Boiler Conversion: Historic Subsidy Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s boiler-conversion assistance was introduced to help qualifying MSMEs in the state’s NCR area move boilers from coal or diesel to PNG, CNG or the cleaner fuels specified in the scheme. The support relates to the conversion project, including eligible material and service costs.

The March 2023 notification describes a two-year scheme period beginning on 23 June 2022. That historic period must be checked against any subsequent extension before a new conversion is budgeted with a subsidy. The continuing need to comply with applicable fuel directions is a separate matter.

sections.title: What the notified support covers
sections.html:
The scheme provides assistance at 30% of eligible conversion expenditure, capped at ₹15 lakh. Its scope concerns existing MSMEs in Haryana’s NCR area and the conversion-related equipment or installation recognised by the notification. It is not a general grant for every new boiler anywhere in Haryana.

A technical assessment should establish the existing fuel, boiler configuration, proposed fuel supply and the work required. Separate the conversion package from unrelated capacity additions or factory expenditure. The supply quotation should make that distinction visible.

sections.title: Prove the change in equipment and fuel
sections.html:
Retain the original boiler particulars, unit registration, location evidence, fuel-supply arrangements, conversion specifications and itemised invoices. Banking records should show the expenditure paid. Commissioning and technical verification should connect the completed work to the proposed cleaner-fuel operation.

A project may also require changes to permissions, safety certification or operating arrangements. Subsidy eligibility does not itself establish compliance with those requirements. Assess both processes before committing to the final equipment design.

For an older claim, assemble the dates of conversion, commercial use, payment and submission together with any acknowledgement or sanction. Those dates determine which notified period and procedure need examination.

Read the March 2023 Boiler Conversion notification. The separate VAT assistance for cleaner fuels concerns fuel expenditure under its own rules, so the two calculations should remain distinct.

title: Haryana Backward and Forward Linkages: 2018 Policy Route
h1: Haryana Backward and Forward Linkages: 2018 Policy Route
description: Distinguish Haryana’s historic food-sector linkage scheme from the discontinued central scheme and prepare project evidence.
metaTitle: Haryana Backward & Forward Linkages: 2018 Policy | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s 2018 food-processing policy included a state scheme for backward and forward linkages in rural areas. Its purpose was to connect the processing business with its supply and market infrastructure. The June 2023 state amendment refers expressly to the scheme notified on 12 June 2019.

This is a separate programme history from MoFPI’s central Creation of Backward and Forward Linkages scheme. The central scheme’s discontinuation date does not, by itself, decide a Haryana state claim.

sections.title: Identify the state approval being relied on
sections.html:
For an older project, begin with the state application or sanction and the implementing notification cited in it. The June 2023 amendment confirms the scheme’s identity but is not a complete statement of eligible components, costs or claim procedure.

Haryana’s 29 May 2026 food policy supersedes the 2018 policy. An existing sanctioned project and a new proposed supply chain therefore require different checks of the applicable version and transition instructions. No current state benefit amount should be inferred from an old central rate.

sections.title: Explain the actual linkage
sections.html:
A useful project description follows the material: who supplies it, where it is collected or handled, what the processor does, and how the finished product reaches its customer. Record the function, capacity and owner of each proposed facility. This helps distinguish a supply-chain investment from an unrelated building or vehicle purchase.

Bring supplier or producer arrangements, customer channels, locations, process details, asset specifications and the financing plan. Itemised costs should identify which component belongs at each stage and whether any other programme has already supported it.

sections.title: Give a pending claim a clear history
sections.html:
Assemble the approved project scope, sanctioned assistance, expenditure and payments, completion evidence, inspection records and departmental correspondence. If implementation changed, identify what changed and whether approval was obtained. A claim can only be assessed meaningfully against the project that the authority actually sanctioned.

title: Haryana Pharmaceutical Capital Subsidy: 2019 Scheme Scope
h1: Haryana Pharmaceutical Capital Subsidy: 2019 Scheme Scope
description: Understand the scope issue in Haryana’s 2019 pharmaceutical capital-subsidy notification before relying on a benefit.
metaTitle: Haryana Pharma Capital Subsidy: 2019 Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s December 2019 pharmaceutical capital-subsidy notification describes assistance towards eligible plant, machinery and technical civil works, but its location scope needs clarification before a project relies on the benefit.

The important question is which location the notification covers. Its opening and general eligibility provisions refer to new units in the Pharma Park at Karnal, while the capital-subsidy subsection uses wider “throughout the State” wording. That difference needs an authoritative interpretation before a unit outside the park relies on this incentive.

sections.title: Establish location and policy period
sections.html:
For a project within the identified pharma park, retain the allotment, site and unit records that demonstrate that location. For a project elsewhere in Haryana, obtain the applicable clarification or sanction basis rather than assuming that the wider sentence settles eligibility.

The notification’s stated period begins with the Pharmaceutical Policy of 6 March 2019 and runs for five years or until an earlier new policy or amendment. A new pharmaceutical investment should not treat the historic rate as currently available without the relevant continuation or successor instructions.

sections.title: Costs and operating conditions
sections.html:
The notification’s stated capital benefit is 25% of the eligible cost, capped at ₹50 lakh. That historic rate remains subject to the location and policy-period questions above.

The notified assistance concerns plant and machinery and technical civil work. A project cost statement should distinguish those components from land, general construction and working capital. Keep itemised invoices, banking payments and the prescribed certification of expenditure.

The notification requires commercial operation and applicable registrations, land-use permissions and pollution-control approvals. An incentive sanction does not substitute for the approvals needed to manufacture a pharmaceutical product.

sections.title: Reviewing a historic project
sections.html:
Bring the production date, original application and sanction, site evidence, cost certification and departmental correspondence together. The original claim process links filing to the start of commercial production, so a timeline is essential. It also matters whether the request concerns eligibility, an unpaid sanctioned amount or a rejected claim.

title: Capital Subsidy for Electric Vehicle Manufacturing
h1: Capital Subsidy for Electric Vehicle Manufacturing
description: Haryana EV capital support concerns qualifying manufacturing investment. Identify the product, enterprise category and assistance head first.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Manufacturing Capital Subsidy: Policy Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml: Haryana’s EV capital-subsidy provision concerns qualifying investment in manufacturing electric vehicles, specified components, batteries and charging infrastructure. It is not a general capital subsidy for every Haryana business, and buying an EV for business use is a different incentive question.

sections.title: Establish what the unit manufactures
sections.html:
The 2022 policy defines EV components and restricts the manufacturing incentives to the relevant exclusive EV or charging-infrastructure use. A component supplier should explain the product, technical function, customer use and manufacturing process. A general-purpose product should not be classified as an EV component simply because one customer is in the automotive sector.

Capital support varies by enterprise category and includes limits on early beneficiaries. The policy treats battery disposal and recycling facilities separately. It also prevents a unit taking the capital benefit from claiming the specified net-SGST investment benefit under the same policy.

sections.title: Prepare the investment case
sections.html:
Build an itemised investment schedule and identify land, building, machinery and other expenditure separately. Keep registrations, product specifications, equipment quotations, ownership details, site records and the production schedule consistent. For an existing enterprise, the additional-investment or complete-conversion conditions must be checked against its actual baseline.

The policy also contains location and category-specific environmental infrastructure conditions. Identify these before choosing a site or finalising the financial model. The application should then follow the operative scheme route with the prescribed certified investment evidence, rather than using a policy table as an approval.

Can the capital and SGST incentives simply be added together?

The policy expressly restricts that combination. Compare the applicable options using the same project assumptions before selecting a benefit. See EV Net SGST Reimbursement.

sections.title: Policy source and application status
sections.html: The notified Haryana Electric Vehicle Policy, 2022 establishes this assistance category. Its stated five-year period and the existence of a policy provision do not establish that a particular application slot remains available. Check the operative scheme notification, amendments and departmental application instructions before committing expenditure on the expectation of support.

title: MoFPI Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure
h1: MoFPI Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure
description: Understand the May 2025 cold-chain scope, integration requirements, grant structure and purchase-timing conditions.
metaTitle: MoFPI Cold Chain Scheme: May 2025 Eligibility | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
MoFPI’s Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure scheme supports a connected processing and temperature-controlled supply chain. The May 2025 revised guideline has a specific scope: non-horticulture products such as dairy, meat, poultry, marine products and fish, with shrimp excluded.

A cold room alone does not establish eligibility. The project needs the required processing and linked infrastructure, designed around the product’s movement through the chain. Older descriptions covering a wider product range should not be used in place of the May 2025 rules.

sections.title: Show how the chain connects
sections.html:
The guideline describes farm-level infrastructure, mandatory processing facilities and the required distribution or transport connections. The application should explain where the raw material comes from, what processing takes place, how temperature is maintained and how finished products reach the market.

Map the capacity of each part. Collection, processing, storage and transport should be proportionate to each other and supported by realistic supply and sales assumptions. A disconnected collection of equipment does not demonstrate an integrated project.

The 2025 guideline excludes expansion or upgradation of an existing project under this route and restricts repeat proposals from entities already assisted under the cold-chain scheme. An applicant’s previous grant history therefore belongs in the first eligibility assessment.

sections.title: Grant structure and expenditure timing
sections.html:
The guideline provides assistance at 35% of eligible project cost in general areas and 50% in difficult areas and for qualifying SC/ST, FPO and SHG projects, capped at ₹10 crore. Rates apply to approved eligible components and relevant cost norms, not automatically to total project expenditure.

It expressly excludes expenditure on eligible components incurred before the Ministry issues the approval letter. The purchase and payment schedule is therefore a funding decision: even a technically suitable machine may fall outside the grant if expenditure occurs too early.

Term-loan, promoter-contribution and net-worth conditions also apply. Category concessions have their own evidence requirements and should be checked separately for each condition. Land, excluded costs and operating finance still need to be funded.

sections.title: Prepare for appraisal and implementation
sections.html:
Assemble the applicant’s ownership and financial records, land documents, process layout, machinery quotations, temperature and capacity specifications, supply arrangements, bank appraisal and funding commitments. Identify the permissions and utilities required for the proposed products and operations.

Applications depend on an applicable EOI and selection. The guideline is not evidence that a fresh window is open. After approval, align procurement and payments with the sanctioned scope, maintain progress and expenditure records, and meet the release conditions. Assistance from another programme cannot duplicate the same component or activity.

Read the May 2025 Cold Chain guidelines. For a horticulture cold-storage project, assess the relevant NHB or NHM/MIDH route on its own terms.

introHtml: The HEEP 2020 employment-generation incentive connects assistance to qualifying jobs created by eligible new units in B, C and D category blocks. A claim must establish both the unit’s eligibility and the employees who satisfy the notified conditions.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. sections.title: Employment has to be evidenced employee by employee

sections.title: Preparing a continuing claim

title: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
h1: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
description: Understand EPCG’s capital-goods duty benefit, export obligation and the records needed from import through discharge.
metaTitle: EPCG Scheme: Capital Goods & Export Obligation | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) scheme can reduce the import-duty cost of eligible capital goods used for exports. The benefit comes with a defined export obligation. The business should assess the expected duty saving and its ability to meet that obligation together.

Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 framework, the ordinary specific export obligation is six times the relevant duties, taxes and cess saved, to be fulfilled over six years from authorisation. Special provisions and later notifications can affect a particular case. The authorisation and applicable Customs notification control the actual benefit.

sections.title: Match the machinery to the export activity
sections.html:
EPCG covers eligible manufacturer exporters, merchant exporters tied to supporting manufacturers and service providers under its rules. Machinery must fit the permitted capital-goods scope and the activity endorsed in the authorisation. Restricted or excluded items require separate treatment.

Before import, prepare the machinery description, classification, supplier quotation, proposed installation location and the goods or services to be exported. The expected duty calculation needs the applicable Customs provisions; “zero duty” should not be treated as a complete landed-cost estimate.

sections.title: Understand both export tests
sections.html:
The specific obligation relates to duty saved. The policy also provides for an average export obligation in applicable cases, based on the preceding export history. Meeting a sales forecast is therefore not necessarily the same as meeting the authorisation’s export conditions.

Model the export schedule against the relevant products, previous performance and eligible evidence. Do not count a shipment merely because it is an export by the group. Its attribution to the authorisation and compliance with the relevant conditions need to be established.

sections.title: Keep evidence through the full life of the authorisation
sections.html:
Retain the authorisation, import documents, duty-saved calculation, installation evidence, machinery particulars and export records. Shipping documents and realisation evidence should support the discharge working. The actual-user condition continues until the export obligation is completed and the discharge certificate is granted.

Where exports fall short or project plans change, assess the available extension, regularisation or payment route under the rules applicable to that authorisation. An unfulfilled obligation can reverse the financial advantage, so review progress while corrective options remain available.

Read Foreign Trade Policy 2023, Chapter 5. EPCG is a trade-policy authorisation with continuing obligations; it should be assessed separately from a state capital or interest subsidy.

title: Haryana Freight Assistance for Exporting MSMEs
h1: Haryana Freight Assistance for Exporting MSMEs
description: Understand the July 2023 Haryana freight-assistance calculation, export evidence and ZED conditions for historic claims.
metaTitle: Haryana Freight Assistance: 2023 Rules & Legacy Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s July 2023 revised Freight Assistance Scheme addressed part of the domestic freight cost incurred by qualifying manufacturing MSMEs exporting their products. It focuses on movement from the manufacturing location to the specified port, air cargo terminal or international border.

The July 2023 revision made ZED certification part of the assistance structure. An export invoice and a freight bill alone do not establish the amount payable.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: How the historic calculation works
sections.html:
The revised notification uses the lower of 1% of the export’s FOB value or actual eligible freight, excluding the specified taxes and charges. Block location and thrust-sector treatment then affect the ceiling. ZED certification level affects the proportion of assistance available.

Each of those stages must be retained in the working. Applying a percentage to total export sales can overstate the claim if the eligible freight is lower, the shipment costs include excluded amounts or the annual ceiling has already been reached.

sections.title: Connect manufacture, shipment and payment
sections.html:
Prepare a shipment schedule linking the goods manufactured by the unit, export invoice, shipping bill, FOB value and domestic transport invoice. Add payment evidence and the relevant export realisation documents. The records should distinguish the domestic eligible leg from international transport and other logistics services.

Keep the Udyam registration, ZED certificate and validity, factory location and block category with the claim. The revised notification also addresses enterprises under common management, so a multi-unit group needs to assess its claim boundary before multiplying unit-level ceilings.

sections.title: Use the revision that governs the period
sections.html:
The July 2023 scheme states an effective date of 1 July 2023. Earlier exports, later claims and investments affected by the 2026 policy transition need their own date assessment. Keep earlier sanctions and claim histories available when establishing the remaining entitlement.

Read the revised Freight Assistance notification and 2026 successor policy. For the costs of exhibiting at an event, see Market Development Assistance, which addresses a different activity.

title: Human Capacity Building: EV Centres of Excellence
h1: Human Capacity Building: EV Centres of Excellence
description: Haryana’s EV policy provides a centre-of-excellence route for skills and capability. Understand the institution’s role and operating proposal.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Centres of Excellence: Skills & Training | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Haryana EV policy’s Centre of Excellence provision supports institutions that can develop skills for the electric-vehicle manufacturing sector. It is an institutional project, rather than a cash payment to each trainee or an ordinary reimbursement of a company’s training bill.

The policy encourages government organisations, PSUs and private companies to establish such centres. It envisages a limited number of supported centres, with a grant divided between establishing the facility and sustaining operations.

sections.title: Show how the centre will serve industry
sections.html:
A credible proposal identifies the skills gap, intended learners, training and technical facilities, industry relationships and how the centre will remain useful after setup. Equipment should follow that operating plan. A list of expensive machines without courses, instructors or a user base does not explain the centre’s purpose.

The policy specifies grant support of 50% of project cost, capped at ₹5 crore for each of five centres. It also describes the split between establishment and operating use and release through annual instalments. The detailed scheme must settle which proposed costs qualify and the conditions attached to release.

sections.title: Prepare the institution and delivery evidence
sections.html:
Collect the applicant’s constitution, governing-body approval, site rights, technical proposal, budget and financing plan. Explain who will own and operate the centre, how trainers will be engaged, which organisations will use it and how outcomes will be recorded. Identify other funding for the same facilities.

The next step is to establish the current selection route and available allocation, then submit the prescribed proposal and answer technical or financial questions. An announced centre and an approved, funded centre are different project states.

Is this the same as an EV R&D grant?

No. Skills and workforce capability are the purpose here. EV R&D support addresses the separate research proposal and its technological objectives.

sections.title: Policy source and application status
sections.html: The notified Haryana Electric Vehicle Policy, 2022 establishes this assistance category. Its stated five-year period and the existence of a policy provision do not establish that a particular application slot remains available. title: Net SGST Investment Subsidy for Haryana Textile Units
h1: Net SGST Investment Subsidy for Haryana Textile Units
description: Understand the textile-specific net SGST calculation, investment limits and evidence needed for a Haryana claim.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Net SGST Subsidy: Calculation & Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s textile investment subsidy links assistance to eligible net State GST paid by the unit. It can support the economics of a qualifying investment over time, but it is not a refund of every GST amount shown on sales invoices.

The July 2023 textile notification contains separate treatment for defined textile categories and block locations. The policy and its schemes were extended to 18 December 2026. A unit’s qualifying investment date, production date and applicable benefit period must still be established.

sections.title: Start with tax actually paid
sections.html:
The notified definition works from net SGST paid through the electronic cash ledger after utilisation of available input tax credit, including relevant IGST credit. Sales tax collected, return liability and cash payment can therefore be different amounts.

The calculation must also relate to the eligible unit and products. Where the business has other activities, branches or an expansion within an existing registration, the records must support the amount attributable to the qualifying investment. A consolidated company return is not a substitute for that reconciliation.

sections.title: The rate is only one part of the benefit
sections.html:
The scheme’s category and location matrix determines the share of eligible net SGST, the number of benefit years and the ceiling linked to fixed-capital investment. These limits must be applied together. A higher headline rate does not establish a larger claim if the eligible cash payment or investment ceiling is lower.

For an expansion, keep the pre-existing assets and output distinguishable from the new investment. The notification imposes conditions on expansion and the incremental benefit; the existing unit’s entire history should not be treated as new eligible expenditure.

sections.title: Records that support a claim
sections.html:
Bring the Udyam and GST registrations, location and block evidence, production records, eligible investment schedule, invoices and proof of payment. Tax working papers should connect filed returns, input-credit utilisation, cash-ledger payments and the proposed subsidy period. Bank and accounting records must support the fixed-capital investment used for the ceiling.

Review the notified claim process and relevant accounting period before filing. Departmental verification of the tax basis and eligibility is part of the claim, so preserve the working rather than only the final figure.

Read the textile net SGST notification and May 2025 extension. This is distinct from the general HEEP net SGST scheme and EV net SGST incentive. Where more than one policy appears relevant, assess the applicable route and overlap conditions before combining amounts.

h1: Haryana Market Development Assistance
description: Understand historic Haryana support for micro and small enterprises participating in eligible national and international exhibitions.
metaTitle: Haryana Exhibition Assistance: 2023 Rules & Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s revised 2023 Market Development Assistance Scheme helped qualifying micro and small enterprises meet specified costs of participating in trade exhibitions. The activity is market access: exhibiting products and meeting buyers at an eligible event. It does not reimburse the value of goods sold or provide a general marketing budget.

The August 2023 revised notification superseded the earlier 2021 scheme. It should be used when examining the event period and claim conditions to which that revision applies.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: The event and expenditure must qualify
sections.html:
The revised scheme provides for assistance towards one national and one international exhibition in a financial year, within its conditions. It addresses eligible participation expenditure and has separate limits for travel and stay. The enterprise category is micro or small; medium status should not be assumed eligible because the wider department serves MSMEs.

The notification’s percentage is subject to component limits and exclusions. For example, assistance for promotional literature does not make the cost of the displayed products eligible. Keep the booth, literature, travel and accommodation costs separately identified.

sections.title: Plan the evidence before travelling
sections.html:
Retain the organiser’s event details, participation confirmation, booth invoice and payment records. Record who represented the enterprise, the travel itinerary and expenditure, and the evidence of actual participation. Product photographs or event records should support what the unit exhibited.

The unit should also preserve its registration, operating location and enterprise classification for the relevant period. If another organisation funded part of the participation, identify that support in the cost working rather than claiming the same expense twice.

sections.title: From participation to claim
sections.html:
Check the applicable event conditions and submission deadline before making bookings. After the event, reconcile each requested amount with eligible expenditure and the notified ceiling. For older participation, assemble the event and filing dates with earlier correspondence so the claim can be examined under the correct revision and transition arrangements.

Read the August 2023 Market Development Assistance notification and 2026 successor policy. Export shipment costs belong under the separate Freight Assistance entry.

title: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
h1: Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
description: Understand MSE-CDP common facilities, infrastructure projects and the ownership and funding model behind a cluster proposal.
metaTitle: MSE-CDP Scheme: Common Facilities & Infrastructure | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
MSE-CDP supports groups of micro and small enterprises through common facilities and industrial infrastructure. The shared investment should address a constraint that member businesses cannot efficiently solve alone, such as testing, a complementary production process or effluent treatment.

The May 2022 guidelines distinguish a Common Facility Centre from an Infrastructure Development project. They have different implementing arrangements and funding patterns. Selecting that component is the first step in building a proposal.

sections.title: A common facility needs committed users
sections.html:
A CFC proposal should show the enterprises that will use it, the common need and demand for its services. The guidelines prescribe an SPV structure, normally a Section 8 company, along with membership and contribution requirements. Larger projects have different contribution and membership provisions.

A state industrial-infrastructure project has a different land and implementing-agency model. A private developer should not assume that the CFC rules make every industrial-estate investment eligible.

sections.title: Funding is shared and project-specific
sections.html:
The programme divides eligible funding between the Government of India, the state and the SPV according to the component, project-cost band and specified location categories. There is no single universal MSE-CDP grant percentage. Projects above a notified ceiling do not automatically receive assistance on their entire cost.

Establish the proposed contributions before finalising the equipment budget. The grant cannot replace the members’ commitment to operate the facility or the implementing agency’s responsibilities for public funds and assets.

sections.title: Prepare the business case for common use
sections.html:
The project report should include a credible demand assessment, technical scope, equipment capacity, land and tenure documents, cost estimates and financing. State and central appraisal stages examine the proposal through the prescribed process; project viability and documented member demand matter alongside formal registration.

The operating plan should identify professional management, staffing, user charges, utilities and maintenance. The guidelines address audit and conflicts involving suppliers or consultants, so procurement and governance arrangements need to be established from the outset.

After approval, keep expenditure, contributions, procurement and utilisation records aligned with the sanctioned project. A functioning centre that serves its intended users is the outcome, rather than simply an installed set of machines.

Read the May 2022 MSE-CDP guidelines and official scheme notices. Haryana’s Mini Cluster scheme is a separate route with different SPV and project rules.

h1: Net SGST Reimbursement for EV Manufacturing
description: Haryana’s EV net-SGST provision depends on eligible manufacturing and tax evidence. Understand its relationship to capital assistance.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Net SGST Reimbursement: Policy Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s Electric Vehicle Policy, 2022 provides a net SGST incentive for qualifying EV manufacturers. It should be distinguished from general industrial SGST investment support and textile investment subsidy in lieu of net SGST.

The EV policy links the benefit to qualifying manufacturers and the defined net-SGST deposit, with a stated period and fixed-capital limit. It also includes a specific alternative for certain cases where cash-ledger SGST is low or the project has an inverted-duty position. That alternative needs its own scheme interpretation; it is not a general tax-refund entitlement.

sections.title: Keep the tax base and investment base separate
sections.html:
GST collected from customers, total GST liability and the relevant net SGST deposit are different figures. Reconcile the claim-year returns, cash and credit ledgers, tax payments and eligible-unit turnover before preparing a subsidy amount. The fixed-capital schedule serves a different purpose: establishing the investment ceiling and applicable project category.

The policy states that a unit taking its EV capital-subsidy benefit cannot take this specified net-SGST benefit. The financing plan should compare the permitted options and document the chosen treatment.

sections.title: Evidence for review
sections.html:
Prepare GST returns and ledgers, reconciled financial statements, product and manufacturing details, site and registration records, commercial-production dates and earlier incentive orders. If one GST registration covers several units or activities, explain the attribution to the qualifying unit rather than using the registration-wide tax total without analysis.

A current application must follow the implementing scheme and relevant annual filing instructions. Paying GST does not replace the incentive application, and a state incentive claim does not alter the tax return obligations.

Is this a refund application under GST law?

It is a state-policy incentive question with its own conditions. Ordinary tax refunds and corrections should be handled through their appropriate tax process.

title: National Horticulture Board Project Assistance
h1: National Horticulture Board Project Assistance
description: Understand NHB’s commercial horticulture and cold-storage routes and prepare a project against the operative guidelines.
metaTitle: NHB Scheme: Horticulture & Cold-Storage Assistance | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
National Horticulture Board assistance includes distinct routes for commercial horticulture and cold-storage projects. The activity, technical design, capacity, financing and applicable guideline determine how a proposal is assessed. “NHB subsidy” is not one rate that can be applied to every horticulture investment.

NHB’s official guideline page lists an amendment dated 21 August 2026 and marks the January 2025 operational guideline as under revision. A new project should establish the operative amended provisions before fixing its eligible cost or purchasing schedule.

sections.title: Select the component before estimating assistance
sections.html:
Describe the crop or commodity, proposed activity, area or capacity, technology and location. A protected-cultivation project, a commercial production project and a cold-storage facility need different technical and cost assessments.

The MIDH framework also distinguishes the NHB route from state horticulture-mission components. Two projects handling the same crop can fall under different routes because their scale or activity differs. The responsible agency should be established before the application is prepared.

sections.title: Build a technically coherent proposal
sections.html:
For production, connect the proposed area, crop cycle, planting material, irrigation and expected output. For a cold store, connect commodity, chamber design, temperature, capacity and handling arrangements. Machinery quotations and civil estimates should follow that design rather than determine it.

Prepare land and tenure evidence, applicant records, the project report, itemised costs, financing and the permissions relevant to the investment. The eligible-cost working must distinguish commercial expenditure from the costs recognised under the applicable component and norms.

sections.title: Coordinate the project and lending records
sections.html:
NHB publishes Letter of Comfort and Grant of Clearance requirements, alongside bank-linked subsidy-claim and inspection formats. Confirm which steps apply to the selected component and project stage. A bank’s loan decision and NHB’s scheme decision have different purposes and should be tracked separately.

During implementation, preserve the original approved scope, expenditure and banking evidence, progress and completion records. The final claim should be reconcilable with the assets and activity that can be inspected. Disclose assistance under other horticulture or government programmes so that the same investment is not presented inconsistently.

For an older sanction, retain the original guideline version and any project-specific amendments. A later published cost norm should not automatically be substituted into a historic approval.

Use the NHB guideline and application requirements page to establish the current source set. See NHM under MIDH for the separate state-mission context.

sections.title: Discuss your horticulture or cold-storage investment
sections.html:
Tell us the crop or commodity, the proposed activity, location, area or capacity, and approximate investment. Include the stage of any bank proposal or existing NHB application so the discussion starts with the work you actually need.

title: National Horticulture Mission under MIDH
h1: National Horticulture Mission under MIDH
description: Understand NHM’s state-level horticulture support and how to identify the right component for a Haryana project.
metaTitle: NHM under MIDH: Haryana Horticulture Project Context | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The National Horticulture Mission, or NHM, is a sub-scheme of the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture. It supports horticulture development through the state-mission framework, with different provisions for production, planting material, protected cultivation and post-harvest infrastructure.

For a Haryana applicant, the practical question is which component the state is implementing for the proposed activity and period. A national cost norm does not, by itself, establish an open local application opportunity or a sanctioned allocation.

sections.title: The component determines the benefit
sections.html:
The MIDH guidelines cover a broad range of horticultural crops and activities. A nursery, a protected-cultivation structure, a pack house and a cold store are assessed against different technical requirements and assistance norms.

The government-to-government funding share for a state programme is not the subsidy percentage payable to an individual applicant. The beneficiary’s assistance must come from the relevant component’s cost and assistance provisions.

sections.title: Match the facility to the horticulture activity
sections.html:
For a post-harvest project, specify the commodity, seasonal volume, handling stages and required capacity. The 2025 framework includes activities such as grading, packing, pre-cooling, storage, ripening and refrigerated movement, with conditions on their design and integration.

Entrepreneur-driven post-harvest projects generally use a credit-linked, back-ended structure under the framework. Specified public or collective applicants have different provisions. Applicant form should therefore be checked alongside the asset, rather than after a subsidy figure has been estimated.

sections.title: Prepare for the state process
sections.html:
Establish the land and tenure, location, crop or commodity, proposed area or capacity, technical specification and financing. Bring the project cost broken into its major components, along with quotations and existing-facility details where relevant. The state’s current application instructions should determine the required sequence of approval, expenditure and verification.

For an existing project, preserve the application, sanction, approved specification, expenditure, payment and inspection records. The claim should demonstrate the approved activity and eligible costs, rather than only the total amount spent.

sections.title: NHM and NHB are separate routes
sections.html:
The MIDH framework assigns specified activities and scales to NHM or NHB. Before choosing either, verify the latest component and capacity boundaries, including subsequent amendments. Do not add their assistance together for the same asset without examining the actual convergence and non-duplication rules.

Read the MIDH Operational Guidelines 2025 and the separate NHB project-assistance explanation. A current Haryana application also needs the operative state instructions and availability for the selected component.

title: PADMA Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme
h1: PADMA Capital Investment Subsidy Scheme
description: PADMA capital support depends on the approved product, cluster relationship and eligible investment. Read the unit-level conditions.
metaTitle: PADMA Capital Subsidy: Unit Eligibility & Investment | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
PADMA capital investment assistance supports qualifying micro and small enterprises linked to Haryana’s approved PADMA products and clusters. It concerns the unit’s eligible plant, machinery and building investment. The implementing agency’s cluster infrastructure grant is covered separately under PCIDS.

The March 2024 notification distinguishes units inside an approved cluster from new units outside it in the relevant block and identified product. Location and product evidence must therefore be established together.

sections.title: Benefit and conditions
sections.html:
Inside a cluster, the notification provides 25% assistance up to ₹25 lakh for other qualifying micro and small units, and 30% up to ₹30 lakh for the specified women, SC or SHG-owned category. It sets different outside-cluster limits and limits the number of supported cases. For an outside-cluster project, obtain confirmation of the applicable percentage and ceiling before including an amount in the investment plan.

The notified period is 17 August 2023 to 16 August 2028, or policy validity. The unit must be engaged in the approved product, meet registration requirements, be in commercial production and continue operating for the stipulated period. The scheme also addresses land tenure, PADMA branding and restrictions on similar capital assistance under other state policies.

sections.title: Evidence for a unit-level application
sections.html:
Prepare documentary confirmation of the cluster and product relationship, land ownership or registered lease, Udyam and HUM records, investment schedule, invoices and commercial-production evidence. An expansion needs the original gross fixed-investment baseline and a clear schedule of additional investment.

The notification links filing to commercial production and specifies a three-month period, subject to its alternative notification dates. Confirm the applicable trigger before commissioning and preserve the complete application acknowledgement. Subsequent inspection and sanction should be recorded as distinct steps.

Does owning a plot establish subsidy eligibility?

No. The unit’s activity, investment, dates and other conditions still need to satisfy the scheme. A developer’s statement is not the unit’s sanction.

title: PADMA Cluster Infrastructure Development Scheme
h1: PADMA Cluster Infrastructure Development Scheme
description: PCIDS supports implementing agencies developing approved Haryana PADMA clusters. Understand infrastructure costs, project ownership and grant conditions.
metaTitle: PADMA Cluster Infrastructure Scheme: PCIDS Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The PADMA Cluster Infrastructure Development Scheme, or PCIDS, supports the implementing agency developing a PADMA cluster. It funds eligible common and basic infrastructure within the approved cluster. A business taking a plot inside that cluster is a different participant and does not automatically become the recipient of the infrastructure grant.

PCIDS was notified on 4 March 2024 under Haryana’s Programme to Accelerate Development for MSME Advancement. The notified period runs from 17 August 2023 to 16 August 2028, or the validity of the PADMA policy. Admission of a particular proposal and the availability of funds still need to be checked separately.

sections.title: What the infrastructure support covers
sections.html:
The scheme identifies basic infrastructure such as internal roads, water and electricity networks, drainage and treatment facilities, alongside PADMA-enabling infrastructure. The proposal must demonstrate how the planned infrastructure serves the cluster and its intended enterprises.

Assistance is linked to the block: the notification specifies 50% in B blocks, 75% in C blocks and 85% in D blocks. It caps assistance at ₹35 crore for clusters up to 50 acres and ₹45 crore for clusters above 50 acres. The minimum land requirement is 25 acres in B and C blocks and 15 acres in D blocks. Funding for B-block projects also has a programme-budget restriction.

These percentages apply to the eligible project cost. Land purchase, preliminary and pre-operative expenditure and working-capital margin are excluded from the grant cost base. The notification addresses how registered land value may count towards the promoter contribution; that is different from using grant money to buy land.

sections.title: The proposal needs an accountable operator
sections.html:
A cluster project is more than a site layout. The implementing agency must establish land control, the target product or enterprise base, infrastructure requirements, financing and the arrangements for completing and operating the facility. Shared infrastructure needs a clear maintenance plan because its value depends on continued service after construction.

Prepare the agency’s constitution and ownership records, land documents, detailed project report, engineering estimates, approvals, means of finance and evidence of the expected user base. The grant is released against the notified process and matching-share requirements. The project cannot be planned on the assumption that government pays every construction invoice upfront.

sections.title: How to approach a PADMA proposal
sections.html:
First confirm the cluster’s status and location category. Then identify the eligible infrastructure components and agency contribution. Develop the detailed proposal and submit through the prescribed departmental route, with the required approvals and project records. During implementation, reconcile work completed, expenditure, the agency’s contribution and grant utilisation.

Does a plot purchase qualify for PCIDS assistance?

PCIDS is directed at the approved implementing agency and cluster infrastructure. An individual manufacturer should separately assess PADMA Capital Investment Subsidy or PADMA Interest Subsidy, where relevant.

Does using the PADMA name establish approval?

No. The project needs documentary evidence of its approved status. A developer’s marketing description is not a government sanction.

sections.title: Assistance is linked to the PADMA product

Prepare the claim through the prescribed department process and retain the acknowledgement. The notification contains different timing language in its application and time-limit clauses. Confirm the controlling deadline promptly rather than waiting for the longer period to expire.

Can the same campaign be claimed under another scheme?

title: PADMA Entrepreneurship Acceleration Scheme
h1: PADMA Entrepreneurship Acceleration Scheme
description: PADMA acceleration supports eligible start-ups working on approved products, with proof-of-concept and commercialisation evidence.
metaTitle: PADMA Entrepreneurship Acceleration: Start-up Eligibility | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
PADMA Entrepreneurship Acceleration is intended for eligible start-ups developing innovative ideas related to approved PADMA product categories. It supports early steps such as proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry and commercialisation.

This is different from routine capital assistance for any newly incorporated business. The proposal must establish the innovation, customer need and route to a viable product or service.

sections.title: What the notification provides
sections.html:
The March 2024 scheme specifies ₹20 lakh assistance for qualifying start-ups inside an approved PADMA cluster and ₹10 lakh outside it in the relevant block around the identified product. It also limits the number of supported start-ups. Those limits mean a policy period through 16 August 2028 does not prove that a place or funding remains available.

The scheme requires recognised start-up status under Haryana’s applicable framework, a registered office in Haryana and a technology-related approach to the identified problem. It excludes an entity formed merely by splitting or reconstructing an existing business from its start-up definition. Similar incentives under other state policies are restricted.

sections.title: Prepare a proposal that can be assessed
sections.html:
Explain the problem, the proposed solution, what has already been demonstrated and what the requested support will achieve. A prototype plan should identify the technical milestone and evidence of success. Market-entry work should identify the intended customer and evidence of demand.

Keep incorporation and recognition records, ownership details, product-category linkage, project budget, existing funding and milestone evidence together. Identify prior government support clearly. Submit the prescribed proposal for departmental and programme examination, and record sanction conditions before spending against an expected award.

Is recognition as a start-up enough?

No. Recognition is one condition. The proposed work must also fit the PADMA category, innovation and other programme requirements.

Does this fund an ordinary machinery expansion?

A routine expansion should be assessed under its relevant investment scheme, such as PADMA Capital Investment Subsidy where its conditions apply. Acceleration support requires the specific early-stage innovation case described in the notification.

title: PADMA Interest Subsidy Scheme
h1: PADMA Interest Subsidy Scheme
description: PADMA term-loan interest assistance differs for units inside and outside approved clusters. Understand borrowing and annual claim evidence.
metaTitle: PADMA Interest Subsidy: Term Loans & Annual Claims | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
PADMA Interest Subsidy reduces the cost of eligible term borrowing for qualifying micro and small enterprises connected to PADMA products. The scheme distinguishes units inside an approved cluster from new units outside it in the relevant block.

The March 2024 notification provides reimbursement at 6% a year or the actual interest rate paid, whichever is lower. The annual ceiling is ₹20 lakh inside the approved cluster and ₹10 lakh for the specified outside-cluster category. It provides for five consecutive financial years, with the starting point linked to the policy and loan dates.

sections.title: The loan and activity must both qualify
sections.html:
The notified scheme period runs from 17 August 2023 to 16 August 2028, or policy validity. Loan sanction and disbursement dates matter; the source includes treatment for a loan sanctioned before re-notification but disbursed afterwards.

The unit must meet registration and operating conditions and must not be a defaulter or NPA with a bank. The source links eligible manufacturing and allied activities to PADMA-approved products and recognises specified supporting services inside clusters. It also restricts similar interest incentives under other state policies.

sections.title: Prepare the annual interest record
sections.html:
Keep the loan sanction, disbursements, bank interest certificate, repayment statement and project investment schedule together. Reconcile the lender’s certificate with interest recorded and paid. The maximum percentage is not a calculation on the original sanctioned loan amount regardless of repayments.

Confirm the approved cluster or outside-cluster product relationship and retain Udyam, HUM and commercial-production evidence. The notification links the annual filing period to the end of the financial year, with the stated alternative for its notification date. Maintain a claim calendar for each year of the support period.

Is working-capital interest included?

The cited benefit is for term loans. PADMA Capital Investment Subsidy addresses a separate investment cost and needs its own assessment. A working-capital facility should not be added without an applicable supporting provision.

Is the entire bank interest bill reimbursed?

No. Assistance is constrained by eligible borrowing, actual interest, the scheme percentage and the annual ceiling. Charges or borrowing outside the approved scope need separate treatment.

title: Patent Fee Reimbursement under Haryana’s EV Policy
h1: Patent Fee Reimbursement under Haryana’s EV Policy
description: The EV patent-fee incentive concerns eligible manufacturing and supported patent expenditure. Separate it from the general Haryana patent scheme.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Patent Fee Reimbursement: Policy Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s EV policy includes reimbursement for qualifying patent-registration expenditure by eligible manufacturing units. The benefit concerns the patent and its permitted costs. It does not give a business ownership of an invention or remove the need to establish the correct applicant and patent rights.

This entry covers the EV-policy provision. The general Haryana Patent Registration Scheme has a different policy basis even though the benefit descriptions may look similar.

sections.title: Identify the patent and the claimant
sections.html:
The policy describes support for domestic and international patent registrations and lists expenditure such as filing, consultancy, search, maintenance and publication fees, subject to a ceiling. The operative scheme must be checked for the treatment and timing of each cost.

Prepare a schedule linking the patent application or registration number, jurisdiction, invention, applicant and the eligible manufacturing unit. If rights sit with a founder, group company or research partner, resolve the ownership and claim relationship before presenting those costs as the unit’s expenditure.

sections.title: Preserve the full expense trail
sections.html:
Keep patent-office acknowledgements and registration documents, professional invoices, official fee receipts, payment evidence and relevant assignments or licences. Separate domestic and overseas costs and identify any other assistance already claimed.

A patent application, examination and registration are different stages. The applicable scheme determines which stage triggers eligibility and filing. Confirm that trigger and the prescribed departmental route instead of assuming that the first legal invoice starts or completes a claim.

Can the same patent expenditure receive both state benefits?

The EV policy restricts similar incentives under other Haryana policies. A cost should be mapped to its chosen assistance head before any claim is filed.

sections.title: Policy source and application status
sections.html: The notified Haryana Electric Vehicle Policy, 2022 establishes this assistance category. Its stated five-year period and the existence of a policy provision do not establish that a particular application slot remains available. Check the operative scheme notification, amendments and departmental application instructions before committing expenditure on the expectation of support.

title: Haryana Patent Registration Assistance
h1: Haryana Patent Registration Assistance
description: Understand the HEEP patent-registration reimbursement, eligible patent expenses and documents for a historic Haryana claim.
metaTitle: Haryana Patent Assistance: HEEP 2020 Reimbursement | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s June 2021 Patent Registration Scheme provided reimbursement of qualifying patent-registration expenditure incurred by eligible MSMEs. It supports the cost of protecting an invention; it does not determine whether the invention is patentable or guarantee that a patent application will succeed.

The June 2021 notification covers domestic and international patent registration. This directory entry is sometimes encountered under the older label “Patent Free”. The official scheme is Patent Registration Assistance.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: What the notification supports
sections.html:
The scheme provides reimbursement of 100% of eligible actual expenditure, subject to a ceiling of ₹25 lakh. The claim remains tied to the eligible patent and notified costs. A general research budget, product-development cost or every professional invoice should not be included without checking its admissibility.

Registration is a material event in the notified process. Filing an application, receiving an examination report and obtaining registration are different stages. Preserve the dates and evidence of each rather than treating an application receipt as proof of a registered patent.

sections.title: Build a patent-specific expense record
sections.html:
Keep the patent application and registration particulars, ownership documents, fee receipts, professional invoices and payments. For international expenditure, preserve the relevant currency and payment evidence. The applicant entity, patent owner and operating unit should be reconciled wherever names or group structures differ.

The unit’s registration, production and eligibility records also form part of the assessment. The historic notification prescribes a short claim period linked to registration, so the filing date must be checked early when reviewing an older patent.

Read the Patent Registration Scheme and 2026 successor policy. The separately documented EV patent incentive has its own policy basis. A patent should not be costed under both routes without examining the applicable overlap conditions.

title: Haryana Cluster Plug and Play Scheme
h1: Haryana Cluster Plug and Play Scheme
description: Understand Haryana’s historic plug-and-play infrastructure model, developer responsibilities and project funding conditions.
metaTitle: Haryana Cluster Plug and Play: Developer Conditions | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s Cluster Plug and Play Scheme was designed to create affordable operating facilities and shared infrastructure for MSMEs. The implementing agency develops the facility and takes responsibility for its common assets. Businesses occupying the premises have their own operating and investment requirements.

The December 2020 notification sits under the MSME Policy 2019. Later extension orders and Haryana’s July 2026 successor policy must be considered when establishing the applicable period for a project. The old programme name alone does not confirm that a new proposal is open for submission.

sections.title: A developer-led operating facility
sections.html:
The scheme’s implementing-agency routes include specified private entities and organisations. The original conditions require at least 10 leasable or saleable plots or operating facilities, with a prescribed reservation for startups and women or SC/ST-owned enterprises.

Land must be arranged through ownership or a qualifying long lease. The original notification also requires minimum own contribution and term lending, each at 20% of project cost. These are financing conditions for the implementing agency, not contributions collected automatically from future occupiers.

sections.title: Common assets create continuing responsibilities
sections.html:
The project can involve enabling infrastructure and capital-intensive common services such as treatment facilities. The implementing agency is responsible for permissions, financial closure, execution, operation and maintenance. The notification requires transparent publication of specified charges and rates.

A proposal should therefore explain how the infrastructure will be used and paid for over time. Identify the expected occupiers, shared services, maintenance costs and the person or organisation accountable for each service.

sections.title: Prepare the project for assessment
sections.html:
Bring land and tenure documents, layout, proposed unit mix, common-facility design, infrastructure estimates and the funding plan. The appraisal needs to distinguish developer-owned assets, plots or premises offered to MSMEs and investment made by those MSMEs themselves.

For a project already approved, retain the sanction, expenditure, progress reports, occupancy arrangements and permissions. Any later claim should reconcile the completed facility with the approved scope and the applicable extension or transition orders.

Read the Cluster Plug and Play notification, published extension order and 2026 successor policy. A member-led common facility may instead raise questions under the separate Mini Cluster scheme.

title: Primary Processing Centre: Identifying the Right Support Route
h1: Primary Processing Centre: Identifying the Right Support Route
description: Define a primary processing centre’s activity and funding route without assuming that the facility name identifies a subsidy scheme.
metaTitle: Primary Processing Centre: Identify the Support Route | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
A primary processing centre is a facility description. It can refer to a place where agricultural produce is collected, cleaned, sorted, graded, packed or handled before further processing or sale. The proposed operations determine which support programme, if any, can apply.

The name “Primary Processing Centre Scheme” is not enough to identify a single verified national or Haryana benefit. A project needs an exact programme, notification and current application route before a grant percentage can be calculated.

sections.title: Describe what happens at the centre
sections.html:
Begin with the incoming commodity, suppliers, seasonal volumes and the condition of the product leaving the facility. List each operation and the equipment required. Distinguish handling and primary processing from manufacture of a finished food product.

Then identify the business model. A producer-owned facility serving members, a commercial service centre and a processor’s collection point may have different applicant and financing conditions even if they use similar equipment.

sections.title: The programme history matters
sections.html:
MoFPI’s central Backward and Forward Linkages scheme included primary processing and collection centres, but it was discontinued from 1 April 2021. Its historic description does not establish a fresh route today.

AMI also needs a current status check: NABARD placed implementation in abeyance from 10 June 2025, pending further orders. The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund has its own eligible-activity and programme-period conditions. These programmes should be assessed individually rather than combined into a generic PPC subsidy promise.

sections.title: Prepare a project that can be mapped accurately
sections.html:
Create a process flow and capacity schedule, identify the site and land tenure, and separate equipment, civil works, utilities, transport and working capital. Add the applicant’s constitution, proposed users or buyers and the financing plan. Explain whether the project is new, already purchased or part of an earlier approval.

Those records allow an adviser to test an actual component against a programme’s rules and identify any timing or overlap issue before expenditure is committed. They also provide a sound basis for the lender’s appraisal, even where no subsidy route is presently established.

Read MoFPI’s historic linkage-scheme scope and NABARD’s AMI status circular. For a project that creates substantive food-processing capacity, the separately defined CEFPPC scheme may be a more relevant question to examine.

title: Purchase Incentives for Electric Vehicle Buyers in Haryana
h1: Purchase Incentives for Electric Vehicle Buyers in Haryana
description: EV buyer incentives depend on vehicle category, purchase and registration evidence, quotas and the current Haryana notification.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Buyer Incentives: Vehicle & Claim Conditions | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s EV buyer incentives address the purchase of specified vehicles by eligible buyers. They are separate from capital assistance for manufacturing EVs, batteries or charging equipment.

The original 2022 policy differentiated battery-electric, fuel-cell and specified hybrid vehicles, with price bands, caps and limits on the number of supported purchases. It also separated purchase assistance from motor-vehicle-tax and registration-fee provisions. A dealer’s combined savings quotation should be broken into those individual benefits.

sections.title: Confirm the exact vehicle before relying on a benefit
sections.html:
Use the vehicle model, technology classification, ex-showroom price, buyer identity, purchase date and Haryana registration details. “Electric” or “hybrid” in a sales description may not establish the precise policy category. Model eligibility and the current list or quota position need direct confirmation under the operative scheme.

The original policy anticipated revisions to incentives and target numbers. Its references to earlier central programmes should not be used as evidence of a current central benefit or a permitted combination today.

sections.title: Records for a buyer’s claim
sections.html:
Keep the dealer invoice, payment evidence, registration certificate, vehicle identification details, buyer records and any subsidy acknowledgement. Establish whether an amount is an invoice discount already received or assistance that still requires a government claim. Preserve the submitted application and any request for clarification.

If a vehicle has already been bought, assess the actual dates and applicable scheme version before making a refund expectation. If the purchase is planned, confirm the current category and filing route first.

Does every EV purchase in Haryana receive a subsidy?

No. Category, dates, quotas and scheme conditions matter. Tax concessions and purchase grants also have separate requirements.

Does the original policy rate prove the amount I will receive?

No. The operative notification, amendments and the claim’s acceptance determine the benefit.

title: Haryana Quality Certification Assistance
h1: Haryana Quality Certification Assistance
description: Assess historic Haryana reimbursement for eligible quality certifications and the evidence supporting certification expenditure.
metaTitle: Haryana Quality Certification: HEEP 2020 Assistance | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s June 2021 Quality Certification Assistance Scheme supported eligible MSMEs obtaining recognised certifications relevant to their products and operations. It addressed the qualifying cost of certification, while the business remains responsible for meeting and maintaining the standard itself.

The June 2021 HEEP notification identifies covered certifications and distinguishes certain country-specific requirements. Choosing the right certificate and accredited provider is part of the preparation, not something the subsidy can resolve afterwards.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: What expenditure is considered?
sections.html:
The notification provides assistance at 75% of eligible expenditure, with a ₹5 lakh ceiling for the listed certification route and a separate ₹10 lakh ceiling for the specified other country-specific certifications. Examples in the notification include ISO, HACCP, BIS, WHO-GMP, ZED and other named standards.

The particular certificate, unit and expense must fit the relevant provision. General factory improvements undertaken to achieve compliance should not automatically be included with certification fees. Itemise the assessment, certification and other proposed costs so their treatment can be checked.

The scheme allows relevant central support within its conditions, but total assistance cannot exceed actual eligible expenditure. Disclose other assistance in the working and retain the sanction and payment records.

sections.title: Documents and application preparation
sections.html:
Assemble the certificate, scope, issue date and validity, the certifying agency’s particulars, invoices and proof of payment. The scope should match the unit and activity for which support is sought. Keep the enterprise’s registration and production records alongside the certification file.

Check the notified application period from the qualifying certification event and preserve the submission acknowledgement. For an existing claim, earlier decisions and the complete expense reconciliation help establish what remains to be considered.

Read the Quality Certification Assistance notification and 2026 successor policy. Buying in-house laboratory equipment is a different expenditure question addressed by Testing Equipment Assistance.

title: R&D Incentives in Haryana’s EV Sector
h1: R&D Incentives in Haryana’s EV Sector
description: Haryana EV research support is for defined technology development and eligible institutions. Prepare milestones, technical evidence and costs.
metaTitle: Haryana EV R&D Incentives: Research & Applicant Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s EV policy provides research-and-development support for specified electric-mobility technology work. It distinguishes new charging technology, new EV technology, research into non-fossil-fuel mobility and R&D infrastructure at eligible educational institutions.

The purpose is a research outcome. Buying standard production machinery or opening an ordinary workshop is not, by itself, evidence of a qualifying R&D project.

sections.title: The applicant and research question matter
sections.html:
The policy describes support for educational or research institutions and selected research centres, with category-specific assistance and limits on the number of proposals. A general “EV innovation” label is insufficient to determine the right category or amount.

A proposal should state the technological problem, existing knowledge, intended improvement, research method and what evidence will demonstrate success. Distinguish a laboratory experiment from a prototype, field trial or commercial production facility.

sections.title: Prepare the project for technical assessment
sections.html:
Record the institution’s constitution, research team, site and facilities, collaboration arrangements, intellectual-property position and proposed budget. Break the work into milestones with measurable outputs. Identify which equipment and personnel costs belong to the research and disclose other public funding.

The relevant implementing scheme and selection instructions should determine the application route, cost treatment and disbursement conditions. Preserve the technical proposal as approved and obtain any required consent before changing the scope. Successful expenditure alone does not prove that the promised research milestone was delivered.

Is a Centre of Excellence automatically an R&D project?

No. A Centre of Excellence may primarily serve skills and training. The actual research objective and applicable category need to be established independently.

Does a private manufacturer qualify on the same terms as a college?

The policy differentiates applicant and activity categories. Use the correct implementing provision rather than assuming one institution’s benefit applies to another.
