title: Haryana Renewable Energy Support: Choosing the Applicable Scheme
h1: Haryana Renewable Energy Support: Choosing the Applicable Scheme
description: Distinguish Haryana’s historic renewable-energy technology support from its separate captive solar and bioenergy project provisions.
metaTitle: Haryana Renewable Energy: Compare the Support Routes | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
A Haryana industrial renewable-energy project can raise two different subsidy questions: support for adopting renewable technology within a unit, or incentives for a qualifying energy-generation project. The equipment, scale and policy version determine which question applies.

The older directory name “Renewable Energy Scheme” does not identify one universal benefit. Two official notifications illustrate why the distinction matters.

sections.title: Renewable technology in an industrial unit
sections.html:
The Revised State Renewable Energy Scheme notified in July 2023 under the MSME Policy 2019 addresses specified renewable-energy technologies used in industry. Its examples include solar photovoltaic and thermal systems, biomass gasifiers, biogas and biomass boilers. The notified assistance is structured around eligible loan interest, with its own annual limit and support period.

A unit assessing this route needs the technology specifications, intended industrial use, term-loan details and evidence of interest paid. The equipment purchase value alone is not the assistance calculation.

sections.title: A qualifying generation project
sections.html:
A separate May 2023 notification under HEEP 2020 addresses captive solar projects above the stated scale and specified agricultural-residue bioenergy projects. It describes industrial or thrust-sector treatment and particular support for eligible bioenergy projects.

A generation project needs an assessment of fuel or energy source, generation capacity, captive use, land, grid or other connection arrangements and the permissions relevant to the installation. These provisions should not be quoted as a general capital subsidy on every factory rooftop system.

sections.title: What to establish for your investment
sections.html:
Prepare a single project note stating the proposed technology, rated capacity, energy use, feedstock where applicable, investment and financing. Identify whether the project is already installed, under a prior sanction or newly proposed. Those facts allow the relevant notification and period to be selected without mixing the two benefit structures.

Both underlying policy histories also need to be considered in light of Haryana’s July 2026 successor policy. Historic terms remain useful for reviewing earlier projects, but a new proposal needs the operative implementing and transition provisions before an amount is included in its financing plan.

Read the Revised State Renewable Energy Scheme, the separate renewable-project notification and the 2026 successor policy.

title: Haryana Research and Development Centre Assistance
h1: Haryana Research and Development Centre Assistance
description: Understand historic Haryana support for R&D centres, eligible project costs and DSIR recognition requirements.
metaTitle: Haryana R&D Centre Assistance: HEEP 2020 Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s June 2021 Research and Development Centre Scheme supported qualifying facilities for developing or improving products, processes, technology, design and quality. The June 2021 notification permits an eligible centre to be standalone or situated within a new or existing enterprise.

The project must demonstrate research activity. Routine production equipment or a quality-control room does not become an eligible R&D centre merely by changing its name.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: Recognition is a release condition
sections.html:
The notification makes recognition by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research, or DSIR, a condition before assistance is released. The research programme, organisation and facility therefore need to be assessed against the recognition route as well as the state incentive.

The centre must also remain operational at disbursement and hold the applicable registrations and permissions. Buying equipment is one stage; establishing and operating the recognised centre is another.

sections.title: What the historic assistance describes
sections.html:
The scheme provides 50% assistance towards eligible project cost, capped at ₹5 crore. Building cost is constrained to a maximum of 25% of project cost within the notified calculation. A detailed cost schedule should distinguish the research facility, machinery and equipment from unrelated manufacturing or office expenditure.

Prepare a description of the proposed research, the products or processes it addresses, the technical team and the role of each major asset. This helps connect the cost estimate to the centre’s actual purpose.

sections.title: Documents and submission
sections.html:
The application file should contain the enterprise and centre particulars, operation date, DSIR recognition evidence, site permissions, asset invoices and payments, and the prescribed cost certification. Keep the research activity record and funding schedule consistent with the project submitted.

The original notification sets a three-month claim period linked to the start of operation or notification, whichever is later. Historic claims need a date assessment, including any applicable delay-condonation or transition provision, rather than an assumption that they remain fileable indefinitely.

title: Seed and Conversion Fund for EV Manufacturing
h1: Seed and Conversion Fund for EV Manufacturing
description: Haryana’s EV conversion fund concerns existing factories changing to EV-related manufacturing, not general start-up seed finance.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Seed & Conversion Fund: Existing Units | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Seed and Conversion Fund in Haryana’s EV policy supports the complete conversion of an existing unit into EV, EV-component or EV-battery manufacturing. Despite the word “seed”, this provision is not a general early-stage start-up fund.

Its policy-level benefit is linked to the book value of plant and machinery in the application year, subject to a percentage and ceiling. Book value is an accounting measure and is different from a supplier’s replacement quotation or the original purchase price of the assets.

sections.title: Establish that a complete conversion is taking place
sections.html:
The proposal needs to show what the unit manufactured before, what it will manufacture afterwards and which assets and processes support the new activity. A small additional EV order in an otherwise unchanged general manufacturing business does not establish complete conversion.

The 2022 policy sets limits on early adopter units within enterprise categories. It also contains location, eligible-product and other manufacturing conditions. The relevant implementing scheme must determine whether the proposed conversion and the timing satisfy those requirements.

sections.title: Prepare the before-and-after evidence
sections.html:
Keep audited accounts and the plant-and-machinery register for the relevant year, depreciation schedules, the conversion plan, product specifications, equipment records and evidence of the old and new production activities. Reconcile the asset values and identify disposals, additions or transfers rather than using an unexplained total from the balance sheet.

Map other assistance claimed on the conversion to avoid overlapping claims under similar state-policy heads. Confirm current quota availability, the application trigger and required certification before submitting the conversion claim.

Can a new factory use this provision instead of capital subsidy?

The conversion fund is framed for existing units converting completely. A new factory needs assessment under the appropriate EV capital-assistance provision.

title: Haryana Textile Skill Training Centre Support
h1: Haryana Textile Skill Training Centre Support
description: Assess assistance for common textile training facilities, eligible implementing agencies and a sustainable training plan.
metaTitle: Haryana Textile Skill Training: Centre Support | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The textile Skill Training Scheme supports the creation of common training facilities. It is relevant to an organisation establishing a centre that can build skills for the textile industry, rather than an employee seeking a personal training payment.

The July 2023 notification defines the implementing agency and eligible project cost. It sits within the textile policy, whose schemes were extended to 18 December 2026. A proposed centre must still meet the scheme’s organisational, location and approval conditions.

sections.title: Who develops the centre?
sections.html:
The notification identifies routes for groups of textile MSMEs through an SPV and for specified associations, skill bodies, government bodies and other qualifying organisations. For the MSME group route, it requires at least five participating units. The applicant’s legal form and membership should be settled before the centre is presented as an eligible project.

The practical starting point is employer demand. Identify the processes taught, the skills employers need, the proposed intake and the equipment required. A training plan should distinguish classroom space from machines, tools and other eligible training infrastructure.

sections.title: What can the assistance cover?
sections.html:
The notified support is 50% of eligible project cost, with ceilings linked to location: ₹2 crore in B blocks, ₹5 crore in C blocks and ₹10 crore in D blocks. Land and building costs are excluded from this assistance.

The centre therefore needs a complete funding plan even where equipment support appears substantial. Premises, working capital, trainers and continuing operations must be funded on their own terms. The grant should be calculated from approved eligible components, not the total cost of establishing the organisation.

sections.title: Prepare for operation as well as sanction
sections.html:
A proposal should include the implementing agency’s constitution, participating employers, site documents, curriculum, equipment specifications, quotations and financing. Explain trainer availability, assessment arrangements and how the centre will recruit learners and meet employer demand.

The centre’s operating plan should identify who maintains the equipment, pays staff and utilities, and tracks training outcomes. Keep procurement, payment and utilisation records so the approved facility can be verified through implementation and claim stages.

Read the textile Skill Training Scheme and the policy extension. For an institution developing skills for EV manufacturing, see the separate EV Centre of Excellence entry. Its applicant, selection and funding conditions need their own assessment.

title: Haryana Mini Cluster Development Scheme
h1: Haryana Mini Cluster Development Scheme
description: Understand Haryana’s common-facility model for micro and small enterprises, SPV funding and project implementation.
metaTitle: Haryana Mini Cluster Scheme: SPV & Common Facilities | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
A mini cluster allows a group of micro and small enterprises to create a common facility that addresses a shared production or service constraint. Haryana’s October 2021 notification supports this collective investment through a member-led special purpose vehicle, or SPV.

The scheme is useful where the members can show a practical need for shared equipment and enough demand to operate it. The starting point is the common problem, such as a missing processing capability, rather than the maximum grant available.

sections.title: A functioning group owns the project
sections.html:
The notification requires functional micro and small enterprises in the relevant cluster and a private limited company as the SPV. It sets different minimum member counts for the prescribed grant bands. Member contributions and responsibilities need to be supported by the company’s records.

This structure differs from the Section 8 organisation specified by the Textile Cluster Development Scheme. The legal form from one programme should not be carried into another application.

sections.title: Project cost and member contribution
sections.html:
The notified model provides 90% state contribution and 10% SPV contribution for an eligible project costing up to ₹5 crore. Assistance is linked to the approved common facility and its conditions. The members still need to arrange their contribution and a viable operating model.

A diagnostic study should establish the cluster’s present capability, demand for the proposed service and the capacity required. The project report should then connect the selected machinery, land arrangements, infrastructure and costs to that finding.

sections.title: Implementation continues after sanction
sections.html:
The SPV must plan procurement, permissions, staffing, maintenance and user charges. The notification requires the facility to become functional within two years of final approval. A practical schedule should account for equipment delivery, installation, utilities and commissioning.

Maintain member resolutions, contribution payments, procurement records and progress reports. A shared facility needs clear access and charging arrangements so that its benefit reaches the intended members and its operating costs can be met.

The original scheme commences from 1 January 2021 and describes continuation until discontinuation by government. Haryana’s 2026 successor MSME policy makes the applicable transition and implementing instructions important for a present-day proposal. Read the Mini Cluster notification before selecting the application route. The central MSE-CDP is separately governed.

title: Haryana VAT Assistance for Industries Using Cleaner Fuels
h1: Haryana VAT Assistance for Industries Using Cleaner Fuels
description: Understand the notified VAT support on PNG and CNG, eligible fuel evidence and the historic scheme period.
metaTitle: Haryana PNG/CNG VAT Assistance: Historic Rules | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Haryana’s December 2022 cleaner-fuel VAT assistance addressed part of the tax paid on qualifying natural-gas purchases by eligible industries. It is an operating-cost incentive. The cost of converting a boiler or installing new equipment belongs to a separate project calculation.

The December 2022 notification describes a two-year period starting on 1 April 2022. A later upload date on the government website does not extend that period. Check any subsequent order before including assistance for later fuel purchases.

sections.title: What the notification says about fuel
sections.html:
The quantum provision provides 50% assistance on VAT paid on natural gas, in piped or compressed form, within the scheme conditions. Although the wider objective discusses cleaner fuels, the claim should follow the fuel specified in the operative assistance provision. LPG or another fuel should not be assumed to receive the same treatment.

The notification covers the specified categories of operating industry and conditions relating to cleaner-fuel use or conversion. The unit’s location, activity and relevant dates should be checked before calculating the tax amount.

sections.title: Work from fuel purchases and tax payment
sections.html:
Prepare a period-wise schedule of gas purchases, quantities, supplier invoices, VAT and banking payments. Reconcile the fuel supplied to the eligible unit’s operation. Where a company has several plants, identify the consumption and purchases attributable to the claiming unit.

Keep the fuel-supply agreement, relevant conversion or commissioning evidence, registrations and permissions alongside the tax working. The claim should make it possible to follow the proposed assistance back to an actual eligible purchase and the applicable period.

sections.title: Reviewing an older claim
sections.html:
Bring earlier submissions, acknowledgements, sanction decisions and correspondence into the file. They establish whether the matter concerns an unfiled historic expense, a pending claim or a release under an existing decision. Each position can require a different procedural assessment.

Read the VAT Assistance notification. For expenditure on the boiler itself, see Boiler Conversion Assistance. Confirm the applicable current fuel directions separately from the subsidy assessment.

title: Haryana Assistance for Electronic Waste Management
h1: Haryana Assistance for Electronic Waste Management
description: Understand the historic Haryana e-waste incentive, its ESDM sector boundary and the records needed for a qualifying project.
metaTitle: Haryana E-Waste Assistance: HEEP 2020 ESDM Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
The Haryana notification titled Assistance for Waste Management has a specific financial-assistance scope: electronic-waste management and e-waste recovery projects for industries in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing sector, or ESDM.

Its general environmental objective should not be read as a subsidy offer for every recycling, municipal-waste or biofuel project. The proposed input material, recovery process and applicant’s sector must fit the operative provisions.

sections.title: Policy period and present-day use
sections.html: This explanation covers the notification issued under HEEP 2020. Haryana notified its Progressive MSME & Export Promotion Policy on 29 July 2026, expressly superseding HEEP 2020. An older claim and a new investment therefore need separate checks of the transition provisions, relevant dates and operative scheme instructions. The historic benefit below should not be entered as an assured receipt in a new project budget.

sections.title: What the historic incentive provides
sections.html:
The October 2021 scheme describes assistance at 50% of eligible project cost, capped at ₹50 crore. Land and building together are subject to a maximum share of 25% of project cost in the calculation. It applies to eligible new ESDM enterprises under its conditions, including specified enterprise scales.

The grant is linked to expenditure and project progress. The notification sets staged releases against defined expenditure milestones. The total assistance should therefore not be modelled as cash available before the promoter begins implementation.

sections.title: Define the recovery project precisely
sections.html:
Prepare the incoming e-waste categories, proposed processing steps, recoverable outputs, residual waste and the capacity of each major system. The machinery and infrastructure estimate should correspond to that process. A mixed-waste business needs a clear separation of the activities proposed for this particular incentive.

Land and building costs should be scheduled separately from machinery, equipment and other expenditure so that the notified limit can be applied. Keep invoices and payment records connected to the approved project components.

sections.title: Permissions and an operating facility
sections.html:
The subsidy does not replace the permissions required to receive, store, process or dispose of the relevant material. The original notification requires applicable registrations and permissions and an operating unit at disbursement. Its statement about the industrial restrictive list does not remove environmental obligations.

For a historic claim, assemble the project dates, land possession, expenditure milestones, operation evidence and earlier approval correspondence. The 2026 policy transition must then be assessed against that history.

Read the Assistance for Waste Management notification and 2026 successor policy. For a different recycling or biofuel investment, begin with the project’s actual process under Subsidy & Incentive Advisory, rather than applying this e-waste rate to an unrelated activity.

title: Water Treatment Incentives for EV Manufacturing
h1: Water Treatment Incentives for EV Manufacturing
description: Haryana’s EV water-treatment provision supports qualifying recycling infrastructure at eligible manufacturing units. Read scope and preparation.
metaTitle: Haryana EV Water Treatment Incentives: Policy Scope | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
This water-treatment incentive is a provision of Haryana’s Electric Vehicle Policy, 2022. It concerns water recycling for qualifying manufacturing plants, rather than a universal subsidy for every water-treatment installation in Haryana.

The policy provides for reimbursement of 50% of the water-treatment plant cost, capped at ₹50 lakh, for a limited number of early units in the medium, large, mega and ultra-mega categories. An MSME label alone is not sufficient: the stated policy categories and the individual implementing scheme must be checked.

sections.title: Explain the water system being installed
sections.html:
Identify the manufacturing process, water intake, wastewater generated, treatment stages and intended reuse. A treatment plant, storage tank, water-softening system and a general plumbing upgrade do not necessarily have the same function or scheme treatment.

The application should connect each claimed cost to the qualifying treatment facility. Keep a technical flow diagram and capacity basis with the equipment specification and civil-work schedule. The authority’s assistance decision is separate from pollution-control compliance and does not replace required consents or operating standards.

sections.title: Records for the claim
sections.html:
Prepare the unit’s product and registration evidence, project category, site documents, treatment design, invoices, payment trail, installation and commissioning records, and any required professional certification. Identify prior support for the same plant and retain the relevant environmental approvals.

Check the current early-beneficiary position and application trigger before relying on reimbursement. For an installed plant, preserve the commissioning date and original submission records so the claim can be assessed against the right version and deadline.

Is any ETP eligible under this EV provision?

No. The enterprise and the facility must fit the applicable EV-policy scheme. Other industries need their own environmental or water-assistance assessment.

sections.title: Related work
sections.html: For the project’s environmental and approval requirements, see Approvals & Compliance. For electronic-waste recovery in the ESDM sector, use the separate Electronic Waste Management Assistance explanation. That scheme does not cover every waste-management asset.

sections.title: Policy source and application status
sections.html: The notified Haryana Electric Vehicle Policy, 2022 establishes this assistance category. title: Change in Land Use (CLU) Approval
h1: Change of Land Use (CLU) Approval in Haryana
description: Understand CLU requirements for a Haryana factory, warehouse or commercial site. Get application, documentation and follow-up support from Rapid.
metaTitle: CLU Approval in Haryana: Process & Documents | Rapid
introHtml:
Put the right land-use permission behind your next factory, warehouse or commercial project. Rapid helps you establish the applicable CLU route, prepare the application and carry the documentation and departmental follow-ups through the agreed assignment.

Start before the building design and land commitment become difficult to change. We work with your site records and proposed activity so the permission being pursued matches the business you intend to run.

sections.title: What is CLU permission?
sections.html:
Change of Land Use permission concerns using land for a purpose different from its permitted use under the applicable planning framework. In Haryana, the first question is the parcel's location, planning jurisdiction and proposed activity. An agricultural revenue entry, an industrial address and an approved industrial use are different pieces of information.

The Town and Country Planning Department publishes controlled-area notifications, development plans and CLU procedures. These establish the route to examine for a particular site. Haryana TCP planning records and services.

sections.title: When should you examine CLU?
sections.html:
Before buying a development site

Check the proposed use and access while the purchase is still being evaluated. A low land price can lose its attraction if the intended facility cannot be developed on the expected basis.

Before a new use or expansion

An existing permission may describe a particular activity, area or layout. A warehouse replacing another use, or an additional parcel beside a factory, needs to be considered against that actual permission.

Before finalising the building investment

Align the land-use position with the architect's proposal and funding assumptions. This gives your team a firmer basis for drawings, project costs and the next approvals.

sections.title: CLU, building approval and ownership: what is the difference?
sections.html:
Question Relevant record or workstream
Who owns or can use the parcel? Title, lease and legal due diligence.
Can the proposed activity use this site? Applicable land-use permission and planning conditions.
Can this building be constructed as designed? Building-plan sanction through the competent authority.
Can vehicles enter from the adjoining road? Road-access review and permission where required.

One application should not be budgeted as a substitute for all four. For construction, continue to Building Plan Approval; for access, see PWD or National Highway access.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
We organise a site-and-use brief, an application checklist and a record of the outstanding inputs. With your appointed professionals, we coordinate the application package, track queries and help assemble responses. You receive visibility of what has been submitted, what is awaited and who needs to act.

The landowner confirms ownership and transaction facts. The architect, surveyor or legal adviser supplies and signs work within their professional responsibility. The department determines permission and conditions. Rapid manages the agreed coordination rather than substituting for those roles.

sections.title: Documents for a useful first review
sections.html:
Bring What it helps establish
Village, district, khasra details and a location pin The exact site and planning jurisdiction.
Current jamabandi, mutation and ownership or lease records The applicant's connection to the land.
Site dimensions, access and available plans Whether the concept fits the parcel and approach.
Proposed activity and approximate built-up area The use for which permission is being considered.
Existing CLU, notices or earlier applications Conditions or issues the new work must address.

The final application follows the department's service checklist. This first-discussion list is not a title-clearance report.

sections.title: How the CLU assignment works
sections.html:
1. Establish the parcel and intended use

Rapid reviews the available records and identifies the jurisdiction and information still needed for the proposed application.

2. Coordinate the application package

The team brings together plans, applicant records and supporting inputs. You confirm the facts and approve the submission.

3. Follow scrutiny and close queries

Rapid tracks the agreed application, routes technical questions to the responsible professional and coordinates documented responses.

4. Hand over the decision and next actions

We explain the permission record and outstanding implementation steps within our scope, so the next workstream starts from the issued conditions.

sections.title: Costs, timing and permission conditions
sections.html:
Budget separately for departmental charges, surveys and professional drawings, legal work and Rapid's advisory fee. A meaningful estimate needs the location, land area, proposed use and stage of the file. Preparation and authority scrutiny are separate parts of the timetable.

The issued permission controls its conditions and implementation requirements. If the project changes or a condition cannot be met on time, review the position before relying on the old permission.

sections.title: Questions about CLU
sections.html:
Is CLU required for every plot in Haryana? No single answer applies to every parcel. Jurisdiction, existing approval and intended use determine the relevant route.

Can I start construction while CLU is being processed? An application acknowledgement is not permission. Establish the approvals required before commencing the proposed work.

Can Rapid review a site before purchase? Yes. We can define a planning-review assignment using the available records, alongside your independent legal and technical due diligence.

What if an earlier application has a query? Share the complete application and correspondence. We can scope the response work around the actual issue instead of starting an unrelated file.

title: PWD Entry & Exit Permission NOC
h1: PWD Entry and Exit Permission in Haryana
description: Plan road access for a Haryana factory or warehouse. Understand the documents, authority checks and PWD application support Rapid provides.
metaTitle: PWD Entry & Exit Permission Haryana | Rapid Consulting
introHtml:
Make vehicle access part of the project plan from the start. Rapid coordinates PWD entry and exit permission work for factories, warehouses and commercial premises, bringing the road details, access drawing and application follow-ups together.

For an owner, the goal is practical: an approach that can serve the facility and is considered through the right road authority. That matters before constructing a gate, drain crossing or heavy-vehicle entrance.

sections.title: What does PWD access permission cover?
sections.html:
Access permission concerns the connection between a property and the adjoining road. It is distinct from owning frontage or having an internal driveway. The review needs to establish who controls the road and what works are proposed at the boundary.

Haryana PWD's published code provides the departmental context for road-related works. Exact access conditions need to be confirmed for the relevant road and permission category. Haryana PWD Code.

sections.title: Which access route fits the site?
sections.html:
Site situation First question
State road or another PWD-controlled road Which PWD office and access requirements apply?
National Highway frontage Does the Ministry/NHAI access route apply instead?
Industrial-estate or municipal road Which estate or local authority controls the connection?
Existing entrance being widened or relocated What does the earlier permission allow, and what changes?

A familiar road name is not enough to identify the authority. For National Highways, see NHAI Entry and Exit Permission.

sections.title: Why plan access early?
sections.html:
Fit the vehicles your business uses

A delivery van, grain truck and articulated trailer need different turning and waiting arrangements. Share expected vehicle sizes with the designer before the gate position is fixed.

Connect access with the site layout

The entrance affects circulation, parking, loading and emergency access. Coordinate it with the building and operating layout instead of treating it as an isolated drawing.

Make the works and budget visible

Drainage, culverts, boundary works and approach construction can affect cost. An early review helps identify which technical inputs and estimates the project needs.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid develops the application brief with your team, identifies the supporting records, coordinates the access proposal prepared by the responsible designer and follows up on the agreed submission. The working file records queries, responses and pending actions.

We coordinate with your surveyor or engineer where technical drawings or calculations are required. Design certification, construction execution and the road authority's decision remain with their respective owners.

sections.title: Documents and site information
sections.html:
Bring Why it matters
Road name, location pin and site frontage Identifies the road and proposed connection.
Ownership or lease and existing permissions Establishes the applicant and previous access position.
Site plan, gate location and photographs Shows how the entrance fits the property.
Vehicle types, loading activity and movement estimate Helps the designer explain the operating need.
Drainage, levels and existing roadside features Identifies matters requiring a technical response.

sections.title: How the access assignment works
sections.html:
1. Confirm the road authority

Establish the location and existing approach. Identify whether the request concerns a new entrance or alteration of an approved one.

2. Prepare the site-specific proposal

Rapid coordinates records and the appointed designer's inputs. The client confirms the operating information and proposed scope.

3. Manage submission and responses

We track the application and coordinate responses to requests for clarification or revised drawings.

4. Carry the conditions into implementation

The issued permission and technical requirements are handed over to the team responsible for the works. Any later change is checked against that record.

sections.title: Fees and expected timing
sections.html: There is no single price that describes every access project. Separate authority charges, technical design, any required approach works and Rapid's fee. The timetable depends on the completed proposal, jurisdiction, queries and any linked land or drainage matters. We explain the preparation milestones after seeing the site details.

sections.title: Questions about PWD permission
sections.html:
Does owning road frontage give me unrestricted access? Do not assume so. Ownership of the plot and permission to connect it to a controlled road are different questions.

Can an existing gate be used for a new factory? Share the earlier permission and proposed traffic. A changed use or heavier movement should be considered explicitly.

Will Rapid build the approach road? This service is application and coordination support. Any design or construction work needs an identified professional or contractor and a separate agreed scope.

Can access and building-plan work run together? They can be coordinated, but dependencies should be established first so the drawings describe the same project.

introHtml:
Prepare your building for the right fire-approval stage with coordinated support from Rapid. We bring the application, building records and professional inputs together, then follow through on the agreed submission and departmental queries.

sections.title: Firefighting scheme or Fire NOC: which do you need?
sections.html:
A firefighting scheme describes the proposed fire-safety arrangements. A Fire NOC relates to the premises and its installed arrangements through the applicable approval process. Renewal or revision addresses a later stage or change.

The governing state legislation is the Haryana Fire and Emergency Services Act, 2022. Identify the applicable approval stage and current requirements against your building's use and design before preparing the application.

sections.title: Match the work to your building's stage

Stage Focus of the discussion
Proposed construction Firefighting scheme, occupancy, layout and access.
Installation or completion Approved arrangements, installed equipment and supporting records.

sections.title: Why coordinate fire approval early?
sections.html:
Avoid expensive layout changes

Staircases, circulation, fire access and storage arrangements are easier to address before construction. Your architect and fire professional should work from the same building proposal.

Prepare for inspection with useful evidence

Equipment photographs alone may not explain whether the complete system is ready. Organise installation and testing records, responsibilities and the approved scheme together.

Keep expansion connected to the original approval

A mezzanine, additional shed or changed storage can affect the review. Bring the change into the application discussion while it can still be planned properly.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid identifies the approval stage with your team, prepares the document checklist and coordinates the application inputs. We maintain the submission and query record, follow up on the file and route technical observations to the responsible professionals.

The fire-system designer and installation team determine and implement the technical solution. The owner keeps the premises and systems ready. Rapid's assignment does not replace design certification, maintenance or the authority's inspection and decision.

sections.title: What does a Forest NOC mean?

Requirement What needs to be established

Tree-felling permission Trees, location, ownership and the applicable permission route.

sections.title: When is an early review useful?

Before finalising the site layout

Before tree removal

sections.title: Documents for the first discussion

Does private ownership mean no forest permission is needed? Ownership and land restrictions are different matters. Check the parcel and proposed activity.

sections.title: What does building-plan approval establish?
sections.html:
Building-plan approval concerns the proposed building and its compliance with the applicable development controls. It differs from permission to use the land and from the occupation certificate considered at completion.

Haryana has different approval jurisdictions. The TCP Department publishes its procedures, while the Urban Local Bodies' OBPAS system has its own building-plan and occupation workflows. Confirm the authority for the parcel before choosing the portal. TCP procedures · ULB OBPAS.

sections.title: New plan, revision or completion?

Your stage Work to examine
New building Site records, applicable controls and proposed drawings.
Extension or additional floor Existing sanction and the full proposed change.
Changed internal layout or use Whether a revised permission or other review is required.
Building already completed As-built records and the occupation-certificate route.

For completion-stage work, see Occupation Certificate. Do not treat a revised drawing as evidence that an unauthorised change has already been accepted.

sections.title: Why coordinate the plan around the business?
sections.html:
Make the building serve the process

Production, storage, loading and people movement should inform the layout. Your design team can address these needs before the plan is submitted.

Keep parallel applications consistent

Building, fire and access records should describe the same premises. Consistency reduces avoidable questions when different professionals work on the project.

Give construction a reliable reference

An issued plan, its conditions and a clear revision record help the project team understand what has been approved.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers

title: Consent To Establish (CTE) HSPCB
h1: Consent to Establish (CTE) from HSPCB
description: Understand CTE requirements, process inputs, documents and costs for a Haryana plant or expansion. Rapid supports applications and query coordination.
metaTitle: HSPCB CTE Haryana: Consent to Establish Support | Rapid
introHtml:
Prepare the environmental permission work before your plant investment moves into establishment. Rapid helps Haryana businesses build a CTE application around the actual process, capacity, utilities and pollution-control arrangements, then coordinates the agreed submission and responses.

Whether you are starting a mill, adding a manufacturing line or setting up a recycling unit, we bring the operating facts into one coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected documents.

sections.title: What is Consent to Establish?
sections.html:
CTE is the establishment-stage consent under the applicable pollution-control framework. For a project requiring consent, it addresses the proposed unit before establishment. HSPCB consent services.

The requirement depends on the activity and current categorisation. Haryana published updated categorisation and consent directions in 2025, including later white-category and green-category orders. An old list or the description “small factory” is not enough to determine the current route. HSPCB policy orders.

sections.title: CTE or CTO: which stage are you at?
sections.html:
Project position Question to resolve
Proposed unit Does the activity require CTE, and what must be prepared before establishment?
Expansion or process change Does the earlier permission cover the new capacity and process?
Plant built and ready to operate What is required for Consent to Operate?
Claimed exempt or white-category activity Which current entry and conditions apply to the exact process?

CTE and CTO are different stages. A CTE application acknowledgement is not an operating permission.

sections.title: What makes a strong CTE application?
sections.html:
A clear process description

Explain the raw material, production steps, finished output and proposed capacity. A metal-cutting workshop and a unit with chemical surface treatment may need different environmental assessment even when both call themselves engineering businesses.

A realistic utilities and emissions picture

Identify water use, wastewater, fuel, stacks and the equipment involved. Your technical team should be able to explain the basis of these figures.

Pollution controls integrated with the project

Treatment and control arrangements affect space, cost and operating responsibilities. Consider them alongside the machinery layout, rather than after equipment procurement.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid creates the input checklist, reviews consistency between the process and project records, coordinates the required technical material and maintains the application/query file. We follow up on the agreed submission and help organise responses from your team and appointed professionals.

The owner confirms the project facts. Technical design, reports and certifications come from the responsible specialists. HSPCB decides the consent and conditions; Rapid coordinates the preparation and follow-through.

sections.title: Documents and information to prepare
sections.html:
Bring Why it is needed
Entity, site and possession records Identifies applicant and location.
Process flow, products and capacity Establishes the proposed activity.
Layout and machinery list Connects the process to the physical facility.
Water, wastewater, fuel and emission estimates Supports environmental inputs and control planning.
Investment/capital records requested for the application Helps establish the fee and declared project basis.
Earlier consent and proposed changes Separates expansion from the existing approved position.

This is a preparation list. The current HSPCB checklist and sector requirements determine the final submission.

sections.title: How the CTE assignment works

Identify the exact process, current permissions and proposed change.

2. Coordinate the application evidence

Rapid brings the project records and technical inputs together and highlights inconsistencies before submission.

3. Submit and respond to scrutiny

The client confirms the facts. Rapid tracks the agreed file and coordinates replies to observations.

4. Carry conditions into establishment

Hand the issued consent and conditions to the project team so the plant is developed on the reviewed basis and can prepare for its next operating stage.

sections.title: Fees, timeline and validity

HSPCB fees depend on the applicable category and fee basis, not Rapid's advisory price. Separate official charges, technical reports and control equipment from our coordination fee. Published departmental service timelines do not include all the time needed to prepare an incomplete project file or implement changes.

The consent order and current directions govern validity and extension. Track those dates against construction and commissioning rather than assuming consent remains valid indefinitely.

sections.title: What is Consent to Operate?
sections.html:
CTO is the operating-stage consent for activities that fall under the applicable consent framework. The review concerns the unit and the conditions under which it may operate. It is different from the establishment-stage CTE.

HSPCB publishes the current consent procedures and orders, including directions concerning first CTO for green-category units and auto-renewal. Those routes have conditions and should not be assumed to cover every applicant. HSPCB consent policy orders.

sections.title: First CTO, renewal or change?

Situation What your team should bring into focus
First application What was permitted, what was installed and what evidence is ready.
Renewal Existing order, expiry, conditions and compliance records.
Additional capacity or different process Whether earlier establishment and operating permissions cover the change.
Name, ownership or other particulars change The record to update and the applicable procedure.

This distinction helps avoid preparing a routine renewal when the plant has materially changed.

sections.title: What helps the operating file progress?
sections.html:
Reconcile the installed plant with its permissions

Compare machinery, products and capacities with earlier records. Identify differences before an officer or laboratory report raises them unexpectedly.

Organise evidence of working controls

The presence of treatment equipment is only part of the picture. Bring operating, monitoring and test information required for the actual application.

Put conditions in front of the responsible team

Consent conditions need continuing attention. Give operations staff a usable record of obligations and dates, rather than leaving the certificate only in an administrative folder.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid reviews the application stage, prepares a document and action list, coordinates the available compliance evidence and follows up on the agreed file. Where observations need a technical response, we bring them to the responsible professional and track the response.

The unit operates and maintains its systems. Laboratories and specialists own their reports; HSPCB owns the consent decision. We do not replace those responsibilities with a promise that a submitted file is an approval.

An owner storing their own goods, a third-party warehouse operator and a business supporting receipt-based finance have different requirements. We define the assignment around that distinction.

sections.title: Development approvals and WDRA registration are different
sections.html:
Development permissions concern the land, building, access and safety of the facility. WDRA registration concerns the regulated warehousing framework associated with negotiable warehouse receipts. The Department of Food and Public Distribution describes WDRA's role and the connection with electronic negotiable warehouse receipts, or eNWRs. Official WDRA overview.

WDRA registration should not be presented as a universal substitute for site approvals or as the only permission every storage shed needs.

Model Questions to settle
Own-stock storage What goods, capacity and building permissions apply?
Storage for customers Who operates the facility and carries responsibility for stock and service?

Cold or specialised storage What additional operating systems and activity-specific requirements apply?

sections.title: What early planning can improve
sections.html:
Make capacity usable

Think about stacking, handling, loading and vehicle access alongside the headline storage area. Your operating and design teams need the same capacity assumptions.

Define responsibility for stored goods

Separate building ownership from warehouse operation and the customer's goods. That helps frame contracts, insurance and registration information.

Connect registration with commercial purpose

If eNWR-based operations are intended, build the registration and operating requirements into the project rather than adding them after construction.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid prepares a facility-development approval brief, identifies the documents for the agreed workstreams and coordinates application follow-ups. The WDRA explanation here helps distinguish that separate registration route; WDRA filing is not included in the development-approval assignment.

Technical design, structural certification, insurance placement and statutory decisions remain with the responsible professionals and authorities. The proposal identifies the development approvals and coordination deliverables included.

sections.title: What to prepare
sections.html:
Record Why it matters
Goods, storage capacity and operating model Defines the actual warehousing business.
Land, lease and building records Establishes possession and facility position.
Layout, equipment and safety arrangements Describes operating readiness.
Operator constitution and financial records Identifies the applicant and financial basis.
Insurance and existing registrations Shows current arrangements and gaps to examine.

WDRA's registration framework includes insurance, net-worth and security-deposit requirements. These are separate from the advisory fee and need the current applicable calculation. Registration rules.

sections.title: How the warehouse assignment works

Agree what will be stored, for whom, at what capacity and whether negotiable receipts are intended.

Rapid connects the project with the relevant site, building and safety services. Any separate registration requirement is identified for the operator's next steps.

3. Coordinate documents and applications

Bring the records and professional inputs together and track the agreed submissions and observations.

4. Prepare the handover for operation

Retain issued documents and identify the conditions and continuing records that belong with the warehouse operator.

sections.title: Costs and timetable
sections.html: Separate authority charges, infrastructure and safety work, insurance, any applicable security deposit and Rapid's fee. A ready existing warehouse and a greenfield development will have different schedules. Registration is also distinct from a bank agreeing to lend against stored goods.

sections.title: Questions about warehouse registration
sections.html:
Does every warehouse need WDRA registration? The answer depends on the operating and receipt model. Establish that first instead of treating every warehouse as an eNWR facility.

Does WDRA registration approve the building? No. Land, building and safety permissions must be addressed through their own applicable routes.

Can a leased warehouse be considered? Bring the lease and operator details so possession, tenure and applicant requirements can be reviewed.

Does registration guarantee customers or finance? Those are separate commercial and lender decisions. Registration supports the relevant regulated activity, not assured occupancy or credit.

description: Understand hazardous-waste authorisation, records and activity-specific requirements in Haryana. Rapid supports documentation and HSPCB coordination.

introHtml:
Put the right authorisation and handling records behind your unit's hazardous-waste activity. Rapid helps identify the relevant waste streams, organise the application and coordinate HSPCB follow-ups for the agreed assignment.

Start with what the process produces or receives: spent oil, process residue, sludge or another identified material. The application should explain the actual waste and its route through the business.

sections.title: What does hazardous-waste authorisation cover?
sections.html:
Authorisation concerns activities regulated under the Hazardous and Other Wastes framework. Generation, storage, treatment, recycling, utilisation and disposal raise different questions. Haryana publishes the applicable rules, application procedure and checklist. HSPCB rules · Authorisation procedure.

The informal name “Hazardous Waste NOC” should not hide which activity and waste category are being authorised.

sections.title: Which situation describes your unit?
sections.html:
Business situation Application focus
Waste generated by your own manufacturing Waste category, quantity, storage and authorised downstream route.
Receiving waste for recycling or recovery Input material, process, capacity and conditions for that activity.
Using a waste as a resource Applicable utilisation procedure and technical requirements.
Renewing or changing an authorisation Existing conditions, actual quantities and the proposed change.

For utilisation, check the relevant HSPCB/CPCB SOP. A permission for one waste or process is not a general permission to handle all materials.

sections.title: Why a waste-specific application matters
sections.html:
Connect the records to the process

Identify where the material arises and how quantities are estimated. This is more useful than describing the whole business simply as “recycling”.

Make storage and movement explainable

The team should know where waste is held, who handles it and where it goes. Consistent records support both the application and day-to-day control.

Avoid confusing separate regulatory routes

CTO, hazardous-waste authorisation and product-specific waste registrations have different purposes. Battery, plastic and e-waste routes should be checked separately for the business's role. HSPCB service distinctions.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid organises a waste-and-activity brief, the document checklist and the agreed application record. We coordinate technical inputs, track queries and help assemble responses. The owner receives a clear view of outstanding records and the responsibilities needed to close them.

The unit remains responsible for actual handling and factual declarations. Authorised operators and technical professionals retain their roles. Rapid does not provide waste transport, disposal or treatment through this application-support service.

sections.title: Documents and records

Site layout and storage arrangements Shows how the material is managed at the premises.
Earlier authorisation and consent orders Identifies conditions and existing scope.
Downstream operator arrangements and relevant records Explains the proposed authorised route.
Testing or technical reports where required Supports classification or utilisation questions.

Use the HSPCB checklist for the final application category.

Land and control

Infrastructure and saleable area

Roads, common services and other development requirements affect the usable plot area and budget. Gross acreage alone does not establish saleable yield.

Development cash flow

Connect land, infrastructure costs and expected receipts to the delivery programme. A licence application and a bankable financial model have related but distinct evidence needs.

sections.title: What is the DDJAY licensing discussion about?

sections.title: What is Haryana Udhyam Memorandum?
sections.html:
HUM is Haryana's enterprise-registration system. The state describes it as a central repository for businesses operating in Haryana, irrespective of size or type, with an Udhyam ID issued through the portal. Haryana MSME Directorate: HUM.

It is different from the national Udyam system used for MSME registration. The similarity in names does not make the records interchangeable.

A scheme application or approval A separate application with its own eligibility and documents.

You are considering a Haryana incentive

Build a management system that your team can use and an independent auditor can assess. Rapid helps Haryana businesses choose a relevant ISO certification scope, prepare documentation and organise the readiness work around the way the business operates.

sections.title: What is ISO certification?
sections.html:
ISO develops standards; it does not issue certificates. An independent certification body audits the relevant management system and makes the certification decision. Rapid's role is preparation and coordination. ISO's explanation of certification.

A management-system certificate concerns the stated organisation, locations and scope. It should not be presented as approval of every product or a replacement for statutory licences.

Business objective Standard family to discuss
Consistent quality and customer requirements ISO 9001, quality management.

Confirm the current edition and transition requirements with the selected certification body. The scope of Rapid's engagement is agreed for the particular standard; this list is not a claim that every specialist certification is delivered in-house. ISO management-system standards.

sections.title: What useful preparation can improve
sections.html:
Make responsibilities visible

Clarify who checks incoming material, releases output, maintains equipment or addresses complaints. A system is stronger when staff know the actions behind the documents.

Reduce repeated quality problems

Use actual rejection, rework and complaint information to identify causes and follow corrective actions. Documentation should support those decisions.

Prepare credible evidence for assessment

Bring procedures, implementation records and reviews together. A generic manual without working evidence does not explain how your business is controlled.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers

Workstream Practical output
Scope and readiness Agreed sites, activities, objective and preparation priorities.
Documentation support A structured set of required documents and evidence responsibilities.
Implementation coordination An action list for the team to close preparation gaps.

Your team implements the system. Auditors and the certification body retain independent responsibility for the assessment and decision. Rapid does not issue an ISO certificate.

sections.title: Documents and evidence to bring
sections.html:
Bring the organisation structure, products/services, locations, process flow, existing procedures, quality or incident records, relevant licences and any customer requirement. If already certified, add the certificate, scope, last audit report and open findings.

For a workshop, inspection and calibration records may be useful. For a warehouse, traceability and stock-handling practices may be central. The final evidence depends on the chosen standard and scope.

Start with the business need and identify the organisation and activities to be assessed.

2. Prepare and implement the system

Rapid coordinates the agreed documentation work; your team puts the required practices into operation and keeps evidence.

3. Review readiness and address gaps

4. Coordinate the audit response

Organise responses to findings within the agreed scope. Maintain the system after certification and plan the certification body's follow-up assessments.

Ask the certification body about its competence, accreditation, scope and recognition for your intended buyer. ISO recommends checking relevant competence and accreditation when choosing a body. A very fast certificate is not evidence of a useful assessment.

The body should state the certification cycle, surveillance and renewal/recertification arrangements. Those are continuing commitments, not merely the initial certificate price.

title: ZED Certification
h1: MSME ZED Certification
description: Understand ZED eligibility, Bronze, Silver and Gold levels, certification costs and subsidies. Get practical assessment-preparation support from Rapid in Haryana.
metaTitle: MSME ZED Certification in Haryana: Costs & Support | Rapid
introHtml:
Build a stronger manufacturing business with ZED certification. Rapid helps Haryana MSMEs choose a suitable certification level, prepare their unit and organise the application and assessment work, with clear responsibility for the support we undertake.

Whether you run a processing unit, engineering workshop or another manufacturing business, start with what you want to improve: product quality, production consistency, workplace practices or readiness for a customer's requirements. We connect that objective to the right next steps.

sections.title: What is ZED certification?
sections.html:
ZED means Zero Defect Zero Effect. The MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification programme assesses manufacturing practices and encourages better quality, productivity and environmental performance. It is a Ministry of MSME initiative implemented by the Quality Council of India (QCI).

For an owner, the practical question is whether the factory can consistently demonstrate how it manages its work. A certificate recognises assessed practices; the preparation should also help your team run the unit better. The programme has three levels: Bronze, Silver and Gold. Official programme overview.

sections.title: What can ZED help your business improve?
sections.html:
ZED connects certification with improvements in day-to-day manufacturing. Use the preparation to strengthen the areas that matter most to your business. Ministry update, August 2026.

Product quality and fewer repeat problems

Use the preparation to examine where defects, rejection and rework occur. For a machining unit, that could mean bringing inspection results and corrective actions together instead of repeatedly addressing the same customer complaint.

More dependable daily operations

Bring attention to maintenance, housekeeping, safety and production responsibilities. The useful result is a working practice that people can follow, with records that show whether it is being followed.

Better use of energy and materials

Look at consumption and waste alongside output. That makes it easier to identify where the unit is losing resources and which improvements deserve attention.

A clearer account of your manufacturing capability

Give customers a clearer picture of how your unit controls quality and manages production. Check which standards a particular buyer needs alongside ZED.

sections.title: Who is eligible, and is ZED compulsory?
sections.html:
Manufacturing MSMEs registered on Udyam are eligible to participate. ZED is voluntary. It does not replace the permissions needed to operate your unit. Eligibility · Programme guidelines.

Before choosing a level, confirm:

  • The enterprise's Udyam details and the manufacturing unit being assessed.
  • The products and processes carried out at that location.
  • Who can provide the unit's operating records and implement improvements.
  • Whether the objective is a first certification, an upgrade or an approaching expiry.

Different units need separate applications. If you operate several facilities, start by identifying the one the assignment will cover. A business doing only trading or services should confirm its applicable route before paying for manufacturing certification support. QCI application process, April 2026, page 6.

sections.title: Bronze, Silver or Gold: which level should you consider?
sections.html:
Choose a level around the practices your unit can demonstrate and the improvements your team is ready to make. A higher badge alone is not a reason to take on a wider assessment.

Level Assessment coverage How to think about the choice
Bronze 7 parameters, including quality, safety, energy and measurement. A starting point for a unit formalising its core practices.
Silver 14 parameters, extending into areas such as process control, maintenance, materials and environment. Consider it when the team can demonstrate a broader operating system.
Gold 20 parameters, adding areas such as supply chain, risk, technology and resource conservation. Consider it when those wider controls are established across the unit.

Parameter coverage follows the September 2024 amendment, Appendix A. The choice guidance is Rapid's practical framing, not an additional eligibility rule.

You can apply for any level after the ZED Pledge if you can meet its requirements. Bronze is not a compulsory first step before Silver or Gold. QCI application process, page 6.

sections.title: What does ZED certification cost?
sections.html:
The published certification charges below are before applicable financial assistance. They are programme charges, not Rapid's consultancy prices.

Certification level Published charge
Bronze ₹8,000
Silver ₹32,000
Gold ₹72,000

These revised amounts took effect on 18 September 2024. The amendment describes the charges as including verification, assessment, certification, monitoring and applicable taxes; it also specifies separate surveillance charges. Official fee amendment, pages 1–2.

For a useful budget, separate four items:

  1. Certification charges: the amount payable through the programme after applicable assistance.
  2. Surveillance: the follow-up assessment obligations during the certificate's life.
  3. Preparation and improvements: for example, testing, calibration, equipment or operating changes your unit needs.
  4. Rapid's advisory fee: the agreed preparation and coordination assignment, quoted separately.

Rapid's fee is quoted after understanding your unit, chosen level and existing systems. Share these details to receive a scope that distinguishes our work from official charges and third-party expenditure.

sections.title: What subsidy and financial assistance are available?
sections.html:
The Ministry's 2025 scheme booklet lists the following certification-cost support:

Enterprise category Listed support on certification cost
Micro 80%
Small 60%
Medium 50%
Eligible women-owned MSMEs 100%

It also lists a ₹10,000 joining reward, which can make Bronze certification free when availed under the scheme. Additional assistance is listed for specified ownership, location and cluster categories. The amount payable depends on the applicant's category and the applicable reward and subsidy rules. Ministry scheme booklet, ZED section.

Support can extend beyond the certificate:

Support category Published maximum
Eligible testing, system or product certification 75% of cost, capped at ₹50,000
Eligible handholding and consultancy Up to ₹2 lakh
Eligible Zero Effect solutions and technology improvements Up to ₹3 lakh

These are separate forms of assistance with their own conditions. They are not an automatic cash payment to every certificate holder, and do not establish that Rapid's fee will be reimbursed. Ministry update, August 2026.

If assistance is a major reason for your project, discuss the proposed spend before commissioning it. The September 2024 amendment makes relevant testing and certification support prospective from ZED registration. Amendment, page 2.

sections.title: What Rapid supports
sections.html:
You should know what your adviser will produce and who is moving each part of the work forward. We define the assignment around your plant and the certification level you want to pursue.

Workstream Rapid's support What you have to work with
Readiness and level selection Review the current process, records and certification objective with your team. A defined scope and list of preparation priorities.
Documentation and awareness Help organise evidence and explain the records and responsibilities needed for the agreed assessment scope. A working document checklist and clearer responsibilities.
Improvement preparation Review progress with the people implementing changes and identify outstanding actions. An action list showing what is ready and what still needs attention.
Application and assessment coordination Support agreed application preparation, evidence organisation and responses to assessment findings. A coordinated record of submissions, queries and next actions.

Your plant team implements operational changes and confirms the facts supplied. Certification is decided through the programme's authorised process. Rapid's role is to help you prepare and coordinate the work, not to issue the certificate.

sections.title: What documents and records should you prepare?
sections.html:
Bring the records you already use. You do not need a polished file before the first conversation. This is a practical preparation checklist; the programme's application and assessment checklist determines the final requirements.

Information to bring Why it matters
Udyam registration, unit address and authorised contact Identifies the applicant and the facility.
Products, process flow and shop-floor photographs Explains what the factory actually does.
Quality checks, rejection and corrective-action records Shows how defects are detected and addressed.
Maintenance and calibration records Shows how equipment reliability and measurement are managed.
Safety arrangements, training and team responsibilities Connects written procedures to people and daily work.
Energy, material-use and relevant environmental records Helps examine resource use and the evidence available.
Existing ISO certificates and earlier assessment reports Identifies useful systems already in place and findings still open.

For an agro processor, discuss the controls around incoming material and the finished product. For an engineering unit, bring inspection and equipment records. The evidence should describe your actual process, not a generic factory.

sections.title: The working sequence
sections.html:
1. Agree the objective and preparation scope

Start with the unit, desired level and business reason for certification. Rapid reviews the starting point with your team and sets out the agreed work and fee.

2. Organise the application and evidence

Complete the programme registration and ZED Pledge, select the level and prepare the required information. Rapid supports the parts agreed in the assignment; your authorised representative confirms the submitted facts.

3. Put improvements into practice

The responsible people at the factory address the identified gaps. We help organise the supporting records and review outstanding preparation so that the assessment is based on work the unit can demonstrate.

4. Complete assessment and respond to findings

The authorised assessment process examines the evidence. Rapid coordinates the agreed response support if further information or corrective action is needed. Your team remains involved in the explanation and closure of findings.

5. Keep the practices working after certification

Retain the certificate and assessment record, track surveillance requirements and keep the underlying systems in use. Discuss any continuing advisory support as a defined follow-on scope.

Applications are made through the official ZED portal. The QCI process document describes registration, verification, assessment and certification.

sections.title: How long does certification take, and how long is it valid?
sections.html:
There is no single turnaround that fits every unit. Preparation, evidence quality, scheduling and closure of findings all affect the completion date. Ask for a plan with separate preparation, submission, assessment and response milestones.

QCI's April 2026 process allows up to five opportunities to close findings within 30 days for Bronze and 60 days for Silver or Gold. These are correction windows, not promised end-to-end delivery times. Certificates are valid for three years. QCI process, pages 6–8.

Bronze has a surveillance assessment after 18 months; Silver and Gold have two surveillance assessments during the cycle. Keep these dates in your compliance calendar. Renewal or a fresh application at expiry must follow the scheme's applicable procedure; it is not automatic. Surveillance amendment · Renewal guidelines, section 3.4.8.

sections.title: Practical questions
sections.html:
Can I apply without a consultant? Yes. The official portal provides the application route. Advisory help is useful when the unit needs support choosing a level, organising evidence, preparing improvements or coordinating responses. Appoint Rapid for a defined need rather than assuming an adviser is compulsory.

Is ZED the same as Udyam registration? No. Udyam records the enterprise's MSME registration. ZED assesses manufacturing practices under its own framework. Having Udyam does not mean the unit has already passed ZED assessment. See our Udyam guide.

We already have ISO certification. Is ZED still relevant? It may be, depending on your business objective. ZED is a separate programme. Certain existing certifications can support parameter exemptions under the framework, subject to accreditation requirements. Bring the certificate and scope so the existing work can be considered. Parameter-exemption notes · ISO support.

Does “free certification” mean the whole project is free? No. Certification-cost assistance does not automatically cover operational improvements, equipment, testing or a private adviser's fee. Ask for each cost category separately, even if the programme charge payable by your unit is zero.

Can ZED replace pollution consent or other factory approvals? No. Certification and permission to operate answer different questions. Keep relevant statutory approvals in place alongside improvement and certification work.

Does Zero Effect mean zero pollution? No. The programme name is an improvement objective, not a literal assurance of zero emissions or complete environmental compliance.

Can Rapid guarantee certification or subsidy? Rapid can take responsibility for the agreed advisory work and follow-through. The authorised bodies determine certification and assistance. We will define our deliverables and the actions your team needs to complete before work begins.

sections.title: Discuss your plant's starting point
sections.html:
Tell us what you manufacture, where the unit is located and whether you are considering Bronze, Silver or Gold. If you are unsure about the level, start with your business objective.

An expert consultant from Rapid will call you to understand the unit and discuss the preparation, scope and next steps. Based in Hisar, we work with businesses across Haryana.
